title.zh: 卷七十四 列傳第六十二: 劉昉 柳裘 皇甫績 郭衍 張衡 楊汪 裴蘊 袁充 李雄
title.en: Volume 74 Biographies 62: Liu Fang, Liu Qiu, Huang Fuji, Guo Yan, Zhang Heng, Yang Wang, Pei Yun, Yuan Chong, Li Xiong
title.raw: 卷七十四 列傳第六十二: 劉昉 柳裘 皇甫績 郭衍 張衡 楊汪 裴蘊 袁充 李雄 Volume 74 Biographies 62: Liu Fang, Liu Qiu, Huang Fuji, Guo Yan, Zhang Heng, Yang Wang, Pei Yun, Yuan Chong, Li Xiong

sentences.zh: 劉昉 柳裘 皇甫績 郭衍 張衡 楊汪 裴蘊 袁充 李雄

translations.literal: Liu Fang, Liu Qiu, Huang Fuji, Guo Yan, Zhang Heng, Yang Wang, Pei Yun, Yuan Chong, Li Xiong
translations.idiomatic: Liu Fang; Liu Qiu; Huang Fuji; Guo Yan; Zhang Heng; Yang Wang; Pei Yun; Yuan Chong; and Li Xiong.

sentences.zh: 列傳第六十二

translations.literal: Biographies 62
translations.idiomatic: Biography 62

sentences.zh: 劉昉柳裘皇甫績郭衍張衡楊汪裴蘊袁充李雄

translations.literal: Liu Fang, Liu Qiu, Huang Fuji, Guo Yan, Zhang Heng, Yang Wang, Pei Yun, Yuan Chong, Li Xiong
translations.idiomatic: Liu Fang, Liu Qiu, Huang Fuji, Guo Yan, Zhang Heng, Yang Wang, Pei Yun, Yuan Chong, and Li Xiong

sentences.zh: 劉昉，博陵望都人也。

translations.literal: Liu Fang was a native of Wangdu in Boling.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Fang came from Wangdu in Boling commandery.

sentences.zh: 父孟良，仕魏，位大司農卿。

translations.literal: His father Mengliang served Wei and held the post of Grand Minister of Agriculture.
translations.idiomatic: His father Mengliang had served Northern Wei and risen to Grand Minister of Agriculture.

sentences.zh: 從武帝入關，為梁州刺史。

translations.literal: Following Emperor Wu into the Pass, he became Governor of Liangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Emperor Wu of Zhou west through the passes and was made governor of Liang province.

sentences.zh: 昉輕狡，有奸數。

translations.literal: Fang was frivolous and cunning, with treacherous schemes.
translations.idiomatic: Fang was flighty and sly, full of underhand designs.

sentences.zh: 周武帝時，以功臣子入侍皇太子。

translations.literal: In the time of Emperor Wu of Zhou, as the son of a meritorious minister he entered service attending the Crown Prince.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Wu of Zhou he entered the palace as a meritorious minister's son to attend the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 及宣帝嗣位，以技佞見狎，出入宮掖，寵冠一時。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xuan succeeded to the throne, through skillful flattery he was treated familiarly, going in and out of the inner palace; his favor surpassed all in that age.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xuan came to the throne, Fang won favor through arts and flattery, passed freely in and out of the inner quarters, and for a time enjoyed unrivaled intimacy.

sentences.zh: 位小禦正，與禦正中大夫顏之儀並見親信。

translations.literal: He held the post of Junior Director of the Imperial Household, and together with Senior Director of the Imperial Household Yan Zhiyi was alike trusted.
translations.idiomatic: He held the junior post of Director of the Imperial Household and, together with the senior director Yan Zhiyi, stood among the emperor's most trusted attendants.

sentences.zh: 及帝不悆，召昉及之儀俱入臥內，屬以後事。

translations.literal: When the Emperor fell ill, he summoned Fang and Zhiyi together into the inner chamber and entrusted them with affairs after his death.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor grew gravely ill, he called Fang and Zhiyi into his sickroom to entrust them with what was to come.

sentences.zh: 帝失喑，不復能言。

translations.literal: The Emperor lost his voice and could no longer speak.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had lost his voice and could no longer speak.

sentences.zh: 昉見靜帝幼沖，又素奇隋文帝。

translations.literal: Fang saw that Emperor Jing was young and tender in years, and had long admired Emperor Wen of Sui.
translations.idiomatic: Fang saw that Emperor Jing was still a child and had long been struck by the stature of Yang Jian, the future Emperor Wen of Sui.

sentences.zh: 時文帝以後父故，有重名於天下，昉遂與鄭譯謀，引帝輔政。

translations.literal: At that time, because the Emperor was father-in-law to the empress, he had great renown throughout the realm; Fang then plotted with Zheng Yi to bring the Emperor in as regent.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Jian, as the empress's father, already enjoyed great renown throughout the realm; Fang therefore joined Zheng Yi in a plan to install him as regent.

sentences.zh: 帝固讓，不敢當，昉曰：「公若為，當速為之。

translations.literal: The Emperor firmly declined, not daring to accept; Fang said: "If you, sir, are to act, you should act quickly.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Jian repeatedly refused, saying he dared not take the role; Fang said, "If you mean to act, sir, act at once.

sentences.zh: 如不為，昉自為也。」

translations.literal: If you do not act, Fang will act himself."
translations.idiomatic: If you will not, then I, Fang, will do it myself."

sentences.zh: 帝乃從之，及帝為丞相，以昉為司馬。

translations.literal: The Emperor then followed his advice; when the Emperor became Chancellor, he appointed Fang as Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Jian yielded; when he became chancellor he made Fang his marshal.

sentences.zh: 時宣帝弟漢王贊居要衝，每與帝同帳而坐。

translations.literal: At that time the Prince of Han, younger brother of Emperor Xuan, held a strategic position and each day sat in the same tent with the Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Han, Emperor Xuan's younger brother, then held a key post at court and sat with Yang Jian in the same tent every day.

sentences.zh: 昉飾美妓進贊，贊甚悅之。

translations.literal: Fang adorned beautiful courtesans and presented them to Zan; Zan was greatly pleased with them.
translations.idiomatic: Fang sent in beautifully adorned courtesans to the prince, who took great delight in them.

sentences.zh: 昉因說贊曰：「大王，先帝之弟，時望所歸。

translations.literal: Fang then urged Zan, saying: "Great King, you are the late emperor's younger brother; the hopes of the age turn to you.
translations.idiomatic: Fang then urged the prince: "Your Highness is the late emperor's own brother, and the realm's hopes rest on you.

sentences.zh: 孺子幼沖，豈堪大事！

translations.literal: The child is young and tender—how can he bear great affairs!
translations.idiomatic: That infant on the throne is far too young to bear the weight of rule!

sentences.zh: 今先帝初崩，群情尚擾，王且歸第。

translations.literal: Now that the late emperor has just died and popular sentiment is still unsettled, Your Highness should for the present return to your residence.
translations.idiomatic: The late emperor has only just died and the realm is still unsettled; withdraw for now to your own residence.

sentences.zh: 待事寧後，入為天子，此萬全計也。」

translations.literal: When affairs are settled, enter and become Son of Heaven—this is a plan of perfect safety."
translations.idiomatic: When all is calm, come in and take the throne yourself—that is the sure plan."

sentences.zh: 贊時年未弱冠，性識庸下，以為信然，遂從之。

translations.literal: Zan was not yet twenty; his nature and understanding were mediocre and low; he believed it true and therefore followed the advice.
translations.idiomatic: The prince was not yet twenty, dull of mind and shallow in judgment; he took Fang at his word and withdrew as urged.

sentences.zh: 文帝以昉有定策功，拜上大將軍，封黃國公，與沛國公鄭譯皆為心膂。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen, because Fang had merit in settling the policy, appointed him Grand General and enfeoffed him as Duke of the State of Huang; together with Duke of Pei Zheng Yi they were both inner confidants.
translations.idiomatic: For his decisive role in the succession, Emperor Wen made Fang grand general and Duke of Huang, and together with Zheng Yi, Duke of Pei, treated both men as his closest confidants.

sentences.zh: 前後賞賜钜萬，出入以甲士自衛，朝野傾矚，稱為黃、沛。

translations.literal: Rewards before and after amounted to tens of thousands; going in and out he was guarded by armored soldiers; court and countryside looked up to him—he was called "Huang and Pei."
translations.idiomatic: Rewards poured in by the tens of thousands; armored guards attended his comings and goings; all eyes at court and in the provinces were on him—and men spoke of "Huang and Pei."

sentences.zh: 時人語曰：「劉昉牽前，鄭譯推後。」

translations.literal: People of the time said: "Liu Fang pulls from the front, Zheng Yi pushes from behind."
translations.idiomatic: A saying of the day ran: "Liu Fang leads from the front, Zheng Yi pushes from behind."

sentences.zh: 昉自恃功，有驕色。

translations.literal: Fang relied on his merit and showed an arrogant bearing.
translations.idiomatic: Fang took pride in his services and carried himself with arrogance.

sentences.zh: 然性粗疏，溺於財利，富商大賈朝夕盈門。

translations.literal: Yet his nature was coarse and careless; he was drowned in wealth and profit, and great merchants morning and evening filled his gate.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he was coarse and careless by nature, greedy for gain, and great merchants thronged his gate from dawn to dusk.

sentences.zh: 于時尉遲迥起兵，帝令韋孝寬討之。

translations.literal: At that time Yuchi Jiong raised troops; the Emperor ordered Wei Xiaokuan to attack him.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuchi Jiong rose in rebellion, the emperor sent Wei Xiaokuan against him.

sentences.zh: 至武陟，諸將不一。

translations.literal: When they reached Wuzhi, the generals were not of one mind.
translations.idiomatic: At Wuzhi the commanders could not agree on a course.

sentences.zh: 帝欲遣昉、譯一人往監軍，因謂之曰：「須得心膂以統大軍，公兩人誰行？」

translations.literal: The Emperor wished to send either Fang or Yi to oversee the army, and therefore said to them: "We need a trusted confidant to command the great army—which of you two will go?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor meant to send either Fang or Yi to supervise the campaign and asked them: "I need a trusted man to take charge of the army—which of you will go?"

sentences.zh: 昉辭未嘗為將，譯以母老為請，帝不懌。

translations.literal: Fang declined, saying he had never been a general; Yi pleaded that his mother was old; the Emperor was displeased.
translations.idiomatic: Fang pleaded that he had never commanded troops; Yi begged off on account of his aged mother. The emperor was displeased.

sentences.zh: 而高熲請行，遂遣之。

translations.literal: Gao Jiong then asked to go, and the Emperor sent him.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Jiong volunteered, and the emperor sent him instead.

sentences.zh: 由是恩禮漸薄。

translations.literal: From this their favor and courtesy gradually grew thin.
translations.idiomatic: From that time their favor at court steadily waned.

sentences.zh: 又王謙、司馬消難相繼反，文帝憂之，忘寢與食。

translations.literal: Moreover Wang Qian and Sima Xiaonan rebelled in succession; Emperor Wen was anxious about it and forgot sleep and food.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Qian and Sima Xiaonan then rose in turn, and Emperor Wen was so troubled that he scarcely ate or slept.

sentences.zh: 昉逸遊縱酒，不以職司為意，相府事多所遺落。

translations.literal: Fang wandered in pleasure and drank freely, not taking his office to heart; many affairs of the Chancellor's office were neglected.
translations.idiomatic: Fang gave himself to pleasure and drink, paid no heed to his duties, and let much of the chancellery's business go undone.

sentences.zh: 帝深銜之，以高熲代司馬。

translations.literal: The Emperor deeply resented this and replaced him as Marshal with Gao Jiong.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor deeply resented this and replaced him as marshal with Gao Jiong.

sentences.zh: 是後益見疏忌。

translations.literal: After this he was increasingly regarded with distance and suspicion.
translations.idiomatic: After that he was increasingly kept at a distance and watched with suspicion.

sentences.zh: 及受禪，進柱國，改封舒國公，閒居無事，不復任使。

translations.literal: When he received the abdication, Fang was promoted to Pillar of State, his fief changed to Duke of the State of Shu, and he lived at leisure with nothing to do, no longer given employment.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Jian took the throne, Fang was made a pillar of state and retitled Duke of Shu, but was left idle and given no further appointments.

sentences.zh: 昉自以佐命元功，中被疏遠，甚不自安。

translations.literal: Fang considered himself a founding minister of the highest merit, yet midway was kept at a distance; he was very ill at ease.
translations.idiomatic: Fang, who had counted himself among the founders of the dynasty, found himself cast aside midway and grew deeply uneasy.

sentences.zh: 後遇京師饑，上命禁酒。

translations.literal: Later, when the capital suffered famine, the sovereign ordered a ban on wine.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when famine struck the capital, the emperor forbade the sale of wine.

sentences.zh: 昉使妾賃屋，當壚酤酒。

translations.literal: Fang had a concubine rent a house and sell wine at the counter.
translations.idiomatic: Fang had a concubine rent a shopfront and sell wine over the counter.

sentences.zh: 治書侍御史梁毗劾奏之，有詔不問。

translations.literal: Secretarial Attendant Imperial Censor Liang Pi impeached him; an edict was issued not to pursue the matter.
translations.idiomatic: The secretarial attendant and imperial censor Liang Pi impeached him, but an edict ordered that the charge not be pursued.

sentences.zh: 昉鬱鬱不得志。

translations.literal: Fang was depressed and could not fulfill his ambitions.
translations.idiomatic: Fang brooded in frustration.

sentences.zh: 時上柱國梁士彥、宇文忻俱失職怨望，時昉並與之交，數相往來。

translations.literal: At that time Senior Pillar Liang Shiyan and Yuwen Xin had both lost their posts and harbored resentment; Fang associated with them both and they frequently visited one another.
translations.idiomatic: The senior pillars Liang Shiyan and Yuwen Xin had both lost office and nursed grievances; Fang joined their circle and they met often.

sentences.zh: 士彥妻有美色，昉與私通，士彥不之知也，情好彌協，遂相與謀反，許推士彥為帝。

translations.literal: Shiyan's wife was beautiful; Fang had a secret affair with her, and Shiyan did not know it; their friendship grew ever closer, and they then plotted rebellion together, agreeing to set up Shiyan as emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Shiyan's wife was beautiful; Fang took her as his lover while Shiyan knew nothing, and their intimacy only deepened until they plotted rebellion together, with Shiyan to be made emperor.

sentences.zh: 後事泄，帝窮問之。

translations.literal: Later the affair leaked out; the Emperor questioned them to the utmost.
translations.idiomatic: When the plot came to light, the emperor interrogated them fully.

sentences.zh: 昉自知不免，默無所封。

translations.literal: Fang knew he could not escape and was silent, offering no defense.
translations.idiomatic: Fang knew there was no escape and answered nothing in his own defense.

sentences.zh: 詔誅之曰：

translations.literal: The edict ordering their execution said:
translations.idiomatic: The edict condemning them read:

sentences.zh: 上柱國郕國公梁士彥、杞國公宇文忻、柱國舒國公劉昉等，朕受命之初，並展勤力，酬勳報效，榮高祿重。

translations.literal: Senior Pillar Duke of Xing Liang Shiyan, Duke of Qi Yuwen Xin, Pillar Duke of Shu Liu Fang, and others—at the beginning when We received the Mandate, all alike exerted their strength; We rewarded their merit and repaid their service with lofty honor and heavy stipends.
translations.idiomatic: Senior pillar Liang Shiyan, Duke of Xing; Yuwen Xin, Duke of Qi; Liu Fang, Duke of Shu; and the rest—at the beginning of Our reign you all labored hard in Our service, and We rewarded your merit with the highest honors and richest stipends.

sentences.zh: 朝夕宴言，備知朕意。

translations.literal: Morning and evening at feast and talk, you fully knew Our mind.
translations.idiomatic: You dined with Us day after day and knew Our mind as well as any man.

sentences.zh: 但心如溪壑，志等豺狼，不荷朝恩，忽謀逆亂。

translations.literal: Yet your hearts were like ravines and gullies, your wills equal to wolves; you did not bear the court's grace and suddenly plotted rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Yet your hearts were bottomless as ravines, your wills wolfish; ungrateful for the court's grace, you suddenly turned to treason.

sentences.zh: 士彥稱有相者，雲其應籙，年過六十，必據九五。

translations.literal: Shiyan claimed there was a physiognomist who said he was destined for the imperial tally; after passing sixty he would surely occupy the Nine-Five position.
translations.idiomatic: Shiyan claimed a physiognomist had told him he was destined for the throne—that after his sixtieth year he would surely take the Nine-Five position.

sentences.zh: 初平尉遲迥，暫臨相州，已有反心，彰于道路。

translations.literal: When Yuchi Jiong was first pacified, he was temporarily placed over Xiangzhou; he already harbored rebellious intent, plain on the roads.
translations.idiomatic: After the defeat of Yuchi Jiong he was briefly made governor of Xiangzhou, but his rebellious intent was already plain to all who passed along the roads.

sentences.zh: 朕即遣人代之，不聲其罪。

translations.literal: We immediately sent someone to replace him, not proclaiming his crime.
translations.idiomatic: We at once sent another to replace him without publicly charging his crime.

sentences.zh: 入京之後，逆意轉深。

translations.literal: After he entered the capital, his rebellious intent grew ever deeper.
translations.idiomatic: Once he came to the capital, his rebellious intent only deepened.

sentences.zh: 忻、昉之徒，言相扶助。

translations.literal: Xin, Fang, and their kind spoke of aiding one another.
translations.idiomatic: Xin, Fang, and their fellows spoke of supporting one another.

sentences.zh: 士彥許率僮僕，克期不遠，欲於蒲州起事。

translations.literal: Shiyan promised to lead his servants; the appointed day was not far off; he wished to raise the affair at Puzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Shiyan promised to lead his household retainers on a day not far off, intending to raise troops at Puzhou.

sentences.zh: 即斷河橋，捉黎陽之關，塞河陽之路。

translations.literal: He would at once cut the river bridge, seize Liyang Pass, and block the Heyang road.
translations.idiomatic: He would cut the Yellow River bridge, seize Liyang Pass, and block the Heyang route.

sentences.zh: 自謂一朝奮發，無人當者，其第二子剛，每常苦諫，第三子叔諧，固深勸獎。

translations.literal: He considered that once he roused himself in a morning, none could withstand him; his second son Gang constantly remonstrated bitterly; his third son Shuhan firmly urged and encouraged him.
translations.idiomatic: He believed that once he struck, none could stand against him; his second son Gang pleaded with him again and again, while his third son Shuhan urged him on.

sentences.zh: 朕既聞知，猶恐枉濫，及授晉部之任，欲驗蒲州之情。

translations.literal: When We had heard and knew, We still feared wrongful punishment; when We appointed him to the Jin region, it was to test his feelings regarding Puzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When We learned of this We still feared to punish wrongly; We appointed him to the Jin region to test his intentions toward Puzhou.

sentences.zh: 士彥得以欣然，雲是天贊。

translations.literal: Shiyan was thereby able to rejoice, saying it was Heaven's aid.
translations.idiomatic: Shiyan rejoiced, calling it Heaven's blessing.

sentences.zh: 忻往定鄴城，自矜不已，位極人臣，猶恨賞薄。

translations.literal: Xin went to settle Ye city and was ceaselessly self-congratulatory; his rank reached the utmost among subjects, yet he still resented that rewards were thin.
translations.idiomatic: Xin had pacified Ye city and never ceased to congratulate himself; though he stood at the summit of subjecthood, he still grumbled that his rewards were meager.

sentences.zh: 朕深念其功，不計無禮，任以武候，授以領軍，寄之爪牙，委之心腹。

translations.literal: We deeply weighed his merit, not reckoning his lack of courtesy; We entrusted him with the Martial Marquisate, appointed him Director of the Palace Guard, entrusted him as Our claws and fangs, and committed him as Our heart and belly.
translations.idiomatic: We weighed his services heavily and overlooked his discourtesy, made him martial marquis, gave him command of the palace guard, and treated him as Our trusted arm and inner confidant.

sentences.zh: 忻密為異計，樹党宮闈，多奏交友，入參宿衛。

translations.literal: Xin secretly made contrary plans, built factions in the inner palace, repeatedly memorialized to bring in friends, and entered to join the night guard.
translations.idiomatic: Xin secretly plotted treason, built a faction in the inner palace, repeatedly recommended his friends for office, and placed them in the night guard.

sentences.zh: 朕推心待物，言必依許。

translations.literal: We treated things with open heart and always granted what was said.
translations.idiomatic: We dealt with him in open trust and granted his every request.

sentences.zh: 為而弗止，心跡漸彰，仍解禁兵，令其改悔。

translations.literal: He acted yet would not stop; heart and tracks gradually showed clear; We still lifted the ban on his troops and ordered him to repent and reform.
translations.idiomatic: He would not stop; his intent grew plain; We even restored his command of troops and urged him to repent.

sentences.zh: 而志規不逞，愈結於懷，乃與士彥情意偏厚，俱營賊逆，逢則交謀。

translations.literal: Yet his ambition could not be fulfilled and bound ever tighter in his breast; he then grew especially close in feeling with Shiyan; both schemed treason; whenever they met they exchanged plots.
translations.idiomatic: Yet his designs went unfulfilled and his resentment only deepened; he grew especially intimate with Shiyan, and together they plotted treason, conferring whenever they met.

sentences.zh: 委士彥河東，自許關右，蒲津事建，即望從征討，兩軍結東西之旅，一舉合連橫之勢，然後北破晉陽，還圖宗社。

translations.literal: He entrusted Shiyan with Hedong and promised himself the land west of the Pass; when the affair at Pujin was established, he at once hoped to follow in the campaign; the two armies would join east-west hosts, and in one stroke combine the power of the horizontal alliance; then they would break Jinyang in the north and turn back to seize the ancestral altars.
translations.idiomatic: Shiyan was to hold Hedong while Xin took the west of the Pass; when the rising at Pujin succeeded, Xin would march to join him, their two armies linking east and west in a single stroke of allied power, then break Jinyang in the north and turn on the imperial house.

sentences.zh: 昉入佐相府，便為非法，三度事發，二度其婦自論。

translations.literal: When Fang entered to assist the Chancellor's office, he at once acted unlawfully; three times the affair broke out, and twice his wife pleaded the case herself.
translations.idiomatic: From the day Fang entered the chancellery he broke the law; three times his crimes came to light, and twice his wife pleaded his case in person.

sentences.zh: 常雲姓是「卯金刀」，名是「一萬日」，劉氏應王，為萬日天子。

translations.literal: He often said his surname was "mao-jin-dao" and his given name was "ten thousand days"; the Liu clan should be king and become Son of Heaven for ten thousand days.
translations.idiomatic: He often said his surname meant "mao metal knife" and his name "ten thousand days"—that the house of Liu was fated to rule as emperor for ten thousand days.

sentences.zh: 朕訓之導之，望其修改。

translations.literal: We instructed and guided him, hoping he would reform.
translations.idiomatic: We admonished and guided him, hoping he would reform.

sentences.zh: 口請自新，志存如舊，亦與士彥情好深重，逆節奸心，盡探肝膈。

translations.literal: With his mouth he asked to renew himself, but his will remained as before; he also was deeply bound in friendship with Shiyan; their treasonous hearts and treacherous wills fully probed each other's inmost parts.
translations.idiomatic: He spoke of reform while his heart stayed unchanged; he was deeply bound to Shiyan, and their treasonous designs were laid bare between them to the last.

sentences.zh: 嘗共士彥論太白所犯，問東井之間，思秦地之亂，訪軒轅之裏，願宮掖之災。

translations.literal: He once discussed with Shiyan the zone violated by the White Planet, inquiring into the space between the Eastern Well stars, thinking of disorder in Qin territory, seeking the precinct of Xuanyuan, and wishing for calamity in the palace quarters.
translations.idiomatic: He once discussed with Shiyan the White Planet's passage, asking what lay between the Eastern Well stars, brooding on turmoil in the Qin lands, seeking the quarter of Xuanyuan, and praying for disaster in the palace.

sentences.zh: 唯侍蒲阪事興，欲在關內應接，殘賊之策，千端萬緒。

translations.literal: He only waited for the affair at Puban to rise, wishing to respond within the Pass; schemes of the destructive rebels were in a thousand and ten thousand strands.
translations.idiomatic: He only waited for the rising at Puban so he could answer from within the Pass; their rebel schemes branched in a thousand ways.

sentences.zh: 惟忻及昉，名位並高，寧肯北面曲躬，臣於士彥？

translations.literal: As for Xin and Fang alone, their fame and rank were both high—would they truly face north and bow low, serving Shiyan as subject?
translations.idiomatic: As for Xin and Fang, both men of the highest rank and standing—would they truly bow north and serve Shiyan as their lord?

sentences.zh: 乃是各懷不遜，圖成亂階，一得擾攘之基，方逞吞併之事。

translations.literal: Rather each harbored insubordination, scheming to complete the steps of disorder; once they gained a foundation of turmoil, they would then display their designs of swallowing and annexing.
translations.idiomatic: Each nursed his own insubordination and meant only to set chaos in motion; once turmoil gave them their opening, they would turn on one another.

sentences.zh: 士彥、忻、昉身為謀首，叔諧贊成父意，議實難容，並已處盡。

translations.literal: Shiyan, Xin, and Fang themselves were the chiefs of the plot; Shuhan supported his father's intent—the deliberation truly could not be borne, and all have been punished to the full.
translations.idiomatic: Shiyan, Xin, and Fang were the ringleaders; Shuhan abetted his father's plot—the case admitted no mercy, and all have been executed.

sentences.zh: 士彥、忻、昉兄弟叔侄，特恕其命。

translations.literal: The brothers, uncles, and nephews of Shiyan, Xin, and Fang were specially spared their lives.
translations.idiomatic: The brothers, uncles, and nephews of Shiyan, Xin, and Fang were specially spared.

sentences.zh: 臨刑，至朝堂，宇文忻見高熲，向之叩頭求哀。

translations.literal: Facing execution, when they came to the court hall, Yuwen Xin saw Gao Jiong and bowed his head to him begging for mercy.
translations.idiomatic: At the execution, when they were brought to the court hall, Yuwen Xin saw Gao Jiong and kowtowed to him for mercy.

sentences.zh: 昉勃然謂忻曰：「事形如此，何叩頭之有！」

translations.literal: Fang angrily said to Xin: "The affair has come to this shape—what is the use of bowing your head!"
translations.idiomatic: Fang burst out at Xin: "Matters stand as they do—what use is kowtowing now!"

sentences.zh: 於是伏誅，籍沒其家。

translations.literal: Thereupon they were executed and their households were confiscated.
translations.idiomatic: They were then executed and their property confiscated.

sentences.zh: 後數日，帝素服臨射殿，盡取三家資物置於前，命百僚射取之，以為鑒戒云。

translations.literal: Several days later the Emperor in plain dress came to the Archery Hall, had all the goods of the three families brought out before him, and ordered the hundred officials to shoot and take them, as a warning lesson.
translations.idiomatic: A few days later the emperor came in plain dress to the Archery Hall, had the goods of all three families set out before him, and ordered the officials to shoot for them as a lesson to the court.

sentences.zh: 柳裘，字茂和，河東解人，南齊司空世隆之曾孫也。

translations.literal: Liu Qiu, styled Maohe, was a native of Jie in Hedong, great-grandson of Shilong, Minister of Works of Southern Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Qiu, courtesy name Maohe, came from Jie in Hedong and was the great-grandson of Shilong, minister of works of Southern Qi.

sentences.zh: 祖惔，梁尚書左僕射。

translations.literal: His grandfather Tan was Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing of Liang.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Tan had been left vice director of the Masters of Writing under Liang.

sentences.zh: 父明，太子舍人、義興太守。

translations.literal: His father Ming was Attendant of the Crown Prince and Administrator of Yixing.
translations.idiomatic: His father Ming had served as attendant of the crown prince and prefect of Yixing.

sentences.zh: 裘少聰慧，弱冠有令名。

translations.literal: Qiu in youth was clever and intelligent; at twenty he had a fine reputation.
translations.idiomatic: Qiu was clever as a boy and by his twentieth year enjoyed an excellent reputation.

sentences.zh: 在梁，歷位尚書郎、駙馬都尉。

translations.literal: Under Liang he successively held the posts of Gentleman of the Masters of Writing and Commandant of Horse Equipage.
translations.idiomatic: Under Liang he rose through the posts of gentleman of the Masters of Writing and commandant of horse equipage.

sentences.zh: 梁元帝為魏軍所逼，遣裘請和于魏。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yuan of Liang was pressed by Wei troops, he sent Qiu to sue for peace with Wei.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yuan of Liang was hard pressed by Wei forces, he sent Qiu to sue for peace.

sentences.zh: 俄而江陵平，遂入關中。

translations.literal: Before long Jiangling was pacified, and he then entered the Guanzhong region.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Jiangling fell, and he passed west into the Guanzhong.

sentences.zh: 周明、武間，自麟趾學士累遷太子侍讀，封昌樂縣侯。

translations.literal: Between the Ming and Wu reigns of Zhou, from Academician of Linzhi he was repeatedly promoted to Reader Attendant to the Crown Prince and enfeoffed as Marquis of Changle County.
translations.idiomatic: Between the reigns of Ming and Wu of Northern Zhou he rose from academician of Linzhi to reader attendant to the crown prince and was enfeoffed as Marquis of Changle.

sentences.zh: 宣帝即位，進爵為公，轉禦飾大夫。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xuan took the throne, his noble rank was advanced to duke and he was transferred to Grand Master of Imperial Adornment.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xuan came to the throne, Qiu was advanced to duke and made grand master of imperial adornment.

sentences.zh: 及帝不悆，留侍禁中，與劉昉、韋暮、皇甫績同謀引隋文帝，曰：「時不可失，今事已然，宜早定大計。

translations.literal: When the Emperor fell ill, he remained to attend within the forbidden quarters; together with Liu Fang, Wei Mu, and Huang Fuji he plotted to bring in Emperor Wen of Sui, saying: "The time must not be lost; the affair is already as it is—you should early settle the great plan.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor fell gravely ill, Qiu stayed within the inner palace and, with Liu Fang, Wei Mu, and Huang Fuji, plotted to install Yang Jian, saying, "The moment must not be lost; the course is already set—you should settle the great design at once.

sentences.zh: 天與不取，反受其殃。」

translations.literal: What Heaven gives and you do not take, you will instead receive its calamity."
translations.idiomatic: Heaven's gift refused becomes Heaven's curse."

sentences.zh: 帝從之。

translations.literal: The Emperor followed this advice.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Jian accepted.

sentences.zh: 進上開府、內史大夫，委以機密。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Upper Opening Grandee and Grand Master of the Palace Secretariat, and entrusted with confidential matters.
translations.idiomatic: Qiu was made upper opening grandee and grand master of the palace secretariat and entrusted with confidential affairs.

sentences.zh: 及尉遲迥作亂，天下騷動，并州總管李穆頗懷猶豫，帝令裘往喻之。

translations.literal: When Yuchi Jiong raised rebellion and the realm was in turmoil, Commander-in-Chief of Bingzhou Li Mu was much hesitant; the Emperor ordered Qiu to go and instruct him.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuchi Jiong rebelled and the realm was in turmoil, Li Mu, commander-in-chief of Bingzhou, wavered; the emperor sent Qiu to persuade him.

sentences.zh: 裘見穆盛陳利害，穆遂歸心。

translations.literal: Qiu saw Mu and fully set forth advantage and harm; Mu thereupon gave his heart.
translations.idiomatic: Qiu laid out the stakes before Li Mu at length, and Mu thereupon gave his allegiance.

sentences.zh: 以奉使功，賜彩三百匹，金九環帶一腰。

translations.literal: For his merit on the mission he was granted three hundred bolts of colored silk and one girdle of gold with nine rings.
translations.idiomatic: For this mission he was rewarded with three hundred bolts of colored silk and a nine-ring gold girdle.

sentences.zh: 時司馬消難奔陳，帝即令裘隨便安集淮南，賜馬及雜物。

translations.literal: At that time Sima Xiaonan fled to Chen; the Emperor at once ordered Qiu to go as convenient to settle and gather Huainan, and granted him horses and various goods.
translations.idiomatic: When Sima Xiaonan fled to Chen, the emperor sent Qiu at once to pacify and settle Huainan, rewarding him with horses and other gifts.

sentences.zh: 開皇元年，進位大將軍，拜許州刺史。

translations.literal: In the first year of Kaihuang he was advanced to Grand General and appointed Governor of Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Kaihuang he was made grand general and governor of Xu province.

sentences.zh: 在官清簡，人懷之，轉曹州刺史。

translations.literal: In office he was pure and simple; the people cherished him, and he was transferred to Governor of Caozhou.
translations.idiomatic: His administration was plain and honest, and the people loved him; he was then transferred to governor of Cao province.

sentences.zh: 後帝思裘定策功，欲加榮秩，將征之，顧朝臣曰：「曹州刺史何當入朝」？

translations.literal: Later the Emperor recalled Qiu's merit in settling the policy, wished to add to his honors and rank, and was about to summon him; he turned to the court ministers and said: "When will the Governor of Caozhou come to court?"
translations.idiomatic: Later the emperor remembered Qiu's role in the succession and meant to honor him with a summons; he asked the court, "When will the governor of Cao province come to the capital?"

sentences.zh: 或曰：「即今冬也。」

translations.literal: Someone said: "This very winter."
translations.idiomatic: Someone answered, "This very winter."

sentences.zh: 乃止。

translations.literal: He then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said no more.

sentences.zh: 裘尋卒，帝傷惜者久之，諡曰安。

translations.literal: Qiu soon died; the Emperor mourned him for a long time and gave him the posthumous title An.
translations.idiomatic: Qiu soon died; the emperor grieved for him a long while and gave him the posthumous name An.

sentences.zh: 子惠音嗣。

translations.literal: His son Huiyin succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Huiyin succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 皇甫績，字功明，安定朝那人也。

translations.literal: Huang Fuji, styled Gongming, was a native of Chaona in Anding.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Fuji, courtesy name Gongming, came from Chaona in Anding commandery.

sentences.zh: 祖穆，魏隴東太守。

translations.literal: His grandfather Mu was Governor of Longdong in Wei.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Mu had been governor of Longdong under Wei.

sentences.zh: 父道，周湖州刺史、雍州都督。

translations.literal: His father Dao was Governor of Huzhou and Area Commander of Yongzhou under Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: His father Dao had served Zhou as governor of Hu province and area commander of Yong.

sentences.zh: 績三歲而孤，為外祖韋孝寬所鞠養。

translations.literal: Fuji was orphaned at three and was reared by his maternal grandfather Wei Xiaokuan.
translations.idiomatic: Fuji lost his father at three and was raised by his maternal grandfather Wei Xiaokuan.

sentences.zh: 孝寬以諸子墮業，督以嚴訓，湣績孤幼，特舍之。

translations.literal: Xiaokuan, because his sons were falling away from their studies, supervised them with stern instruction, but pitied Fuji as orphaned and young and specially exempted him.
translations.idiomatic: Because his own sons were neglecting their studies, Xiaokuan kept them under strict discipline, but pitied the orphaned Fuji and exempted him.

sentences.zh: 績歎曰：「我無庭訓，養於外氏，不能克躬勵已，何以成立！」

translations.literal: Fuji sighed and said: "I have no instruction in my own household; I am reared in my mother's clan—if I cannot restrain myself and urge myself on, how can I establish myself!"
translations.idiomatic: Fuji sighed and said, "I have no father's teaching at home and am raised in my mother's house—if I cannot discipline myself, how can I ever make my way!"

sentences.zh: 深自感激，命左右自杖三十。

translations.literal: Deeply moved, he ordered his attendants to beat him thirty strokes.
translations.idiomatic: Deeply stirred, he ordered his attendants to flog him thirty strokes.

sentences.zh: 孝寬聞而對之流涕。

translations.literal: When Xiaokuan heard of it he wept facing him.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiaokuan heard of it, he wept before him.

sentences.zh: 於是專精好學，略涉經史。

translations.literal: Thereupon he devoted himself to study and came to have some acquaintance with the classics and histories.
translations.idiomatic: From then on he devoted himself to learning and gained some knowledge of the classics and histories.

sentences.zh: 周武帝為魯公時，引為侍讀。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu of Zhou was Duke of Lu, he was brought in as Reader Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: When the future Emperor Wu of Zhou was still Duke of Lu, Fuji was made his reader attendant.

sentences.zh: 建德初，轉宮尹中士。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Jiande reign he was transferred to Palace Master Gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Jiande era he became palace master gentleman.

sentences.zh: 武帝嘗避暑雲陽宮，時宣帝為太子監國。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu once took the cool at Yunyang Palace; at that time Emperor Xuan as Crown Prince supervised the state.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu once retired to Yunyang Palace for the summer while the crown prince, the future Emperor Xuan, supervised the realm.

sentences.zh: 衛剌王作亂，城門已閉，百僚多有遁者。

translations.literal: Prince Wei of Ci raised rebellion; the city gates were already closed, and many among the hundred officials had fled.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Wei of Ci rebelled, the city gates were shut and many officials fled.

sentences.zh: 績聞難赴之，於玄武門遇皇太子，下樓執績手，悲喜交集。

translations.literal: Fuji heard of the crisis and hastened to it; at the Xuanwu Gate he met the Crown Prince, who came down from the tower, seized Fuji's hand, and joy and sorrow mingled together.
translations.idiomatic: Fuji heard of the crisis and rushed to the palace; at the Xuanwu Gate he met the crown prince, who came down from the tower, seized his hand, and wept and rejoiced together.

sentences.zh: 帝聞而善之，遷小宮尹。

translations.literal: The Emperor heard and approved, and promoted him to Junior Palace Master.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor heard and approved, and promoted him to junior palace master.

sentences.zh: 宣政初，錄前後功，封義陽縣男，累轉禦正下士。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Xuanzheng reign his services before and after were recorded; he was enfeoffed as Baron of Yiyang County and repeatedly transferred to Junior Director of the Imperial Household.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Xuanzheng era his past services were recognized with a barony in Yiyang county, and he rose to junior director of the imperial household.

sentences.zh: 宣帝崩，隋文帝總己，績有力焉。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xuan died, Emperor Wen of Sui took personal charge of affairs, and Fuji had strength in it.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xuan died and Yang Jian took power, Fuji had played an important part.

sentences.zh: 加上開府，轉內史中大夫，進封郡公。

translations.literal: He was advanced to Upper Opening Grandee, transferred to Grand Master of the Palace Secretariat, and his fief was advanced to Duke of a Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He was made upper opening grandee and grand master of the palace secretariat and advanced to commandery duke.

sentences.zh: 拜大將軍。

translations.literal: He was appointed Grand General.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed grand general.

sentences.zh: 開皇元年，出為豫州刺史。

translations.literal: In the first year of Kaihuang he went out as Governor of Yuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Kaihuang he was sent out as governor of Yu province.

sentences.zh: 尋拜都官尚書。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made minister of justice.

sentences.zh: 轉晉州刺史。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Governor of Jinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was then transferred to governor of Jin province.

sentences.zh: 將之官，稽首言陳有三可滅。

translations.literal: As he was about to take up his post, he bowed his head and said Chen had three reasons why it could be destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: Before taking up his post he kowtowed and said Chen could be conquered for three reasons.

sentences.zh: 帝問其狀，績曰：「大吞小，一也。

translations.literal: The Emperor asked the particulars; Fuji said: "The great swallowing the small—this is the first.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked what he meant; Fuji said, "First, the great may swallow the small.

sentences.zh: 以有道伐無道，二也。

translations.literal: Using the Way to attack the unprincipled—this is the second.
translations.idiomatic: Second, the righteous may strike the unrighteous.

sentences.zh: 納叛臣蕭岩，於我有詞，三也。

translations.literal: Harbouring the rebel minister Xiao Yan gives Us grounds for complaint—this is the third.
translations.idiomatic: Third, they have given us cause by sheltering the rebel minister Xiao Yan.

sentences.zh: 陛下若命鷹揚之將，臣請預戎行。」

translations.literal: If Your Majesty orders soaring-hawk generals, your servant asks to join the campaign."
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty sends forth your hawk generals, I beg to march with them."

sentences.zh: 上嘉勞而遣之。

translations.literal: The sovereign praised and comforted him and sent him on his way.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised him and sent him to his post.

sentences.zh: 陳平，拜蘇州刺史。

translations.literal: When Chen was pacified, he was appointed Governor of Suzhou.
translations.idiomatic: After Chen fell, he was made governor of Su province.

sentences.zh: 高智慧作亂江南，州人顧子元等發兵應之，因以攻績，相持八旬。

translations.literal: Gao Zhihui raised rebellion in Jiangnan; men of the province such as Gu Ziyuan raised troops in response and thereby attacked Fuji; they faced one another for eighty days.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Zhihui rebelled in the south, Gu Ziyuan and others of the province rose to join him and besieged Fuji for eighty days.

sentences.zh: 子元素感績恩，於冬至日遣使奉牛酒。

translations.literal: Ziyuan had long felt Fuji's kindness; on the winter solstice he sent envoys offering oxen and wine.
translations.idiomatic: Ziyuan, moved by Fuji's past kindness, sent oxen and wine on the winter solstice.

sentences.zh: 績遺之書。

translations.literal: Fuji sent him a letter.
translations.idiomatic: Fuji sent him a letter in reply.

sentences.zh: 子元得書，於城下頓首陳謝。

translations.literal: Ziyuan received the letter and below the wall bowed his head and declared his repentance.
translations.idiomatic: Ziyuan received the letter and kowtowed beneath the walls to express his remorse.

sentences.zh: 楊素援兵至，合擊破之。

translations.literal: Yang Su's relief troops arrived; joining forces they defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Su's relief force arrived, they joined and broke the rebels.

sentences.zh: 拜信州總管。

translations.literal: He was appointed Commander-in-Chief of Xinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was made commander-in-chief of Xin province.

sentences.zh: 俄以病乞骸骨，詔徵還京師，賜以禦藥，中使相望，顧問不絕。

translations.literal: Soon, on grounds of illness, he requested to retire; an edict summoned him back to the capital, granted him imperial medicine, and palace envoys followed one another in unbroken inquiry and care.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he asked to retire on grounds of illness; the emperor summoned him to the capital, sent imperial physicians, and palace envoys came in an unbroken stream to inquire after him.

sentences.zh: 卒于家，諡曰安。

translations.literal: He died at home; his posthumous title was An.
translations.idiomatic: He died at home and was given the posthumous name An.

sentences.zh: 子偲嗣。

translations.literal: His son Si succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Si succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 大業中，位尚書主爵郎。

translations.literal: In the Daye era he held the post of Gentleman in Charge of Fiefs in the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: In the Daye era he served as gentleman in charge of fiefs in the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 郭衍，字彥文，自雲太原介休人也。

translations.literal: Guo Yan, styled Yanwen, claimed to be from Jiexiu in Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Yan, courtesy name Yanwen, said his family came from Jiexiu in Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 父崇，以舍人從魏孝武帝入關，位侍中。

translations.literal: His father Chong, as Attendant, followed Emperor Xiaowu of Wei into the Pass and reached the post of Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: His father Chong had followed Emperor Xiaowu of Wei west through the passes as an attendant and risen to palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 衍少驍武，善騎射。

translations.literal: Yan in youth was valiant in battle and skilled in horsemanship and archery.
translations.idiomatic: Yan was bold and skilled in horsemanship and archery from youth.

sentences.zh: 建德中，以軍功累遷儀同大將軍。

translations.literal: In the Jiande era, through military merit he was repeatedly promoted to General of the Same Rank.
translations.idiomatic: During the Jiande era he rose through military merit to general of the same rank.

sentences.zh: 又從周武帝平并州，以功加開府，封武強縣公，賜姓叱羅氏。

translations.literal: He also followed Emperor Wu of Zhou in pacifying Bingzhou; for merit he was given the Opening Office, enfeoffed as Duke of Wuqiang County, and granted the surname Chiluo.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Emperor Wu in the conquest of Bing province, was given the opening office, enfeoffed as Duke of Wuqiang, and granted the surname Chiluo.

sentences.zh: 宣政元年，為右中軍熊渠中大夫。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xuanzheng he was Grand Master of the Xiongqu in the Right Central Army.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Xuanzheng he became grand master of the Xiongqu in the right central army.

sentences.zh: 尉遲迥之亂，從韋孝寬討之，以功授上柱國，封武山郡公。

translations.literal: In Yuchi Jiong's rebellion he followed Wei Xiaokuan in attacking him; for merit he was granted Senior Pillar of State and enfeoffed as Duke of Wushan Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuchi Jiong's rebellion he campaigned under Wei Xiaokuan and was made senior pillar of state and Duke of Wushan commandery.

sentences.zh: 密勸隋文帝殺周室諸王，早行禪代，由是大被親昵。

translations.literal: He secretly urged Emperor Wen of Sui to kill the princes of the Zhou house and carry out the abdication early; thereby he was greatly treated with intimacy.
translations.idiomatic: He secretly urged Yang Jian to kill the Zhou princes and seize the throne quickly, and for this won great intimacy with him.

sentences.zh: 開皇元年，衍復舊姓為郭氏。

translations.literal: In the first year of Kaihuang, Yan restored his former surname Guo.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Kaihuang he resumed the surname Guo.

sentences.zh: 突厥犯塞，以衍為行軍總管，領兵屯平涼。

translations.literal: When the Turks raided the frontier, Yan was made campaign commander and led troops stationed at Pingliang.
translations.idiomatic: When the Turks raided the frontier, Yan was made campaign commander and stationed at Pingliang.

sentences.zh: 數歲，虜不入境。

translations.literal: For several years the barbarians did not enter the borders.
translations.idiomatic: For several years the barbarians did not cross the border.

sentences.zh: 徵為開漕渠大監。

translations.literal: He was summoned to be Grand Supervisor of Opening the Transport Canal.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled to serve as grand supervisor of opening the transport canal.

sentences.zh: 部率水工，鑿渠引渭水，經大興城北，東至潼關，漕運四百餘里，關中賴之，名曰富人渠。

translations.literal: He directed water workers, cut a canal to draw the Wei River past the north of Daxing city east to Tong Pass—grain transport for more than four hundred li; Guanzhong relied on it, and it was named the Rich Men's Canal.
translations.idiomatic: He led the water workers in cutting a canal from the Wei River north of Daxing east to Tong Pass, a transport route of more than four hundred li on which Guanzhong depended; it was called the Rich Men's Canal.

sentences.zh: 五年，授瀛州刺史，遇秋霖大水，其屬縣多致漂沒，人皆上高樹，依大塚。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was appointed Governor of Yingzhou; he encountered autumn rains and great floods, and many subordinate counties were washed away; people all climbed tall trees and clung to great mounds.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he was made governor of Ying province; autumn floods drowned many of its counties, and people took refuge in tall trees and on great mounds.

sentences.zh: 衍親備船筏，並齊糧食拯救之，民多獲濟。

translations.literal: Yan personally prepared boats and rafts, and together with grain and food rescued them; many among the people were saved.
translations.idiomatic: Yan himself prepared boats and rafts and brought grain to rescue them; many lives were saved.

sentences.zh: 衍先開倉賑恤，後始聞奏。

translations.literal: Yan first opened the granaries for relief, and only afterward reported it.
translations.idiomatic: Yan opened the granaries for relief before reporting to the throne.

sentences.zh: 上大善之，遷授朔州總管。

translations.literal: The sovereign greatly approved and transferred him to Commander-in-Chief of Shuozhou.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor greatly approved and made him commander-in-chief of Shuo province.

sentences.zh: 所部有恆安鎮，北接蕃境，常勞轉運。

translations.literal: In his jurisdiction was Heng'an Fort, north adjoining the barbarian frontier, which constantly strained transport.
translations.idiomatic: His jurisdiction included Heng'an Fort on the northern frontier, where transport was a constant burden.

sentences.zh: 衍乃選沃饒地，置屯田，歲嬴萬餘石，人免轉輸之勞。

translations.literal: Yan then selected fertile land and established military colonies; each year the surplus was more than ten thousand piculs, and the people were spared the labor of transport.
translations.idiomatic: Yan chose fertile land for military colonies that yielded more than ten thousand piculs a year and spared the people the burden of transport.

sentences.zh: 又築桑乾鎮，皆稱旨。

translations.literal: He also built Sanggan Fort—all met with imperial approval.
translations.idiomatic: He also built Sanggan Fort—all to the emperor's satisfaction.

sentences.zh: 十年，從晉王廣出鎮揚州。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he followed Prince Jin Guang in going out to garrison Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year he followed Prince Jin Yang Guang to Yangzhou as his garrison commander.

sentences.zh: 遇江表構逆，命衍為總管，先屯京口。

translations.literal: When the region south of the Yangzi raised rebellion, he was ordered as commander-in-chief and first encamped at Jingkou.
translations.idiomatic: When the south rose in rebellion, he was made campaign commander and encamped first at Jingkou.

sentences.zh: 于貴洲南與賊戰，敗之。

translations.literal: South of Guizhou he fought the rebels and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: South of Guizhou he fought the rebels and defeated them.

sentences.zh: 仍討東陽、永嘉、宣城、黟、歙諸洞，盡平之。

translations.literal: He then attacked the cave settlements of Dongyang, Yongjia, Xuancheng, Yi, and She, and pacified them all.
translations.idiomatic: He then pacified the mountain strongholds of Dongyang, Yongjia, Xuancheng, Yi, and She.

sentences.zh: 授蔣州刺史。

translations.literal: He was appointed Governor of Jiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was made governor of Jiang province.

sentences.zh: 衍臨下甚倨，事上甚卑。

translations.literal: Yan toward those below was very arrogant; toward his superiors very humble.
translations.idiomatic: Yan was haughty toward those below and obsequious toward those above.

sentences.zh: 晉王愛昵之，宴賜隆厚。

translations.literal: Prince Jin loved and favored him; feasts and gifts were lavish.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Jin favored him and lavished feasts and gifts upon him.

sentences.zh: 遷洪州總管。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Commander-in-Chief of Hongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to commander-in-chief of Hong province.

sentences.zh: 王有奪宗之謀，托衍心腹，遣宇文述以情告之。

translations.literal: The Prince had a plan to seize the succession and entrusted Yan as his intimate; he sent Yuwen Shu to tell him his mind.
translations.idiomatic: The prince plotted to seize the succession and made Yan his confidant; he sent Yuwen Shu to disclose his intentions.

sentences.zh: 衍大喜曰：「若所謀事果，自可為皇太子。

translations.literal: Yan was greatly pleased and said: "If the affair you plan succeeds, you may naturally become Crown Prince.
translations.idiomatic: Yan was delighted and said, "If your plan succeeds, you will naturally become crown prince.

sentences.zh: 如其不諧，亦須據淮海，復梁、陳之舊。

translations.literal: If it does not succeed, you must still hold the Huaihai region and restore the old domains of Liang and Chen.
translations.idiomatic: If it fails, you must still hold the Huaihai and restore the old domains of Liang and Chen.

sentences.zh: 副君酒客，其如我何！」

translations.literal: The deputy ruler and the wine guest—what can they do to me!"
translations.idiomatic: As for the crown prince and his wine companions—what can they do to us!"

sentences.zh: 王因召衍，陰共計議。

translations.literal: The Prince thereupon summoned Yan and secretly planned together.
translations.idiomatic: The prince then summoned Yan and they plotted in secret.

sentences.zh: 又恐人疑無故來往，托以妻患癭，王妃蕭氏有術能療之。

translations.literal: They also feared people would suspect their coming and going without cause, and used as a pretext that Yan's wife suffered from goiter and that the prince's consort, the Lady Xiao, had skill to cure it.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing suspicion at their constant visits, they claimed Yan's wife had goiter and that the prince's consort Lady Xiao could cure it.

sentences.zh: 以狀奏帝，聽共妻向江都，往來無度。

translations.literal: They reported this to the Emperor, who permitted them to bring their wives to Jiangdu; their comings and goings were without limit.
translations.idiomatic: They reported this to the emperor, who allowed their wives to travel to Jiangdu; thereafter they came and went without restraint.

sentences.zh: 衍又詐稱廣州俚反，王乃奏衍行兵討之。

translations.literal: Yan also falsely claimed that the Li of Guangzhou had rebelled; the Prince then memorialized that Yan should march to attack them.
translations.idiomatic: Yan also falsely reported a Li rebellion in Guangzhou, and the prince memorialized that Yan should march to suppress it.

sentences.zh: 由是大修甲仗，陰養士卒。

translations.literal: Thereby he greatly repaired armor and weapons and secretly nurtured soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: On this pretext he greatly expanded his arms and secretly trained troops.

sentences.zh: 及王入為太子，徵授左監門率，轉左宗衛率。

translations.literal: When the Prince entered the capital as Crown Prince, Yan was summoned and appointed Left Director of the Gate Guards, then transferred to Left Director of the Palace Guard.
translations.idiomatic: When the prince became crown prince, Yan was summoned as left director of the gate guards and then left director of the palace guard.

sentences.zh: 文帝于仁壽宮將大漸，太子與楊素矯詔令衍、宇文述領東宮兵，帖上臺宿衛，門禁並由之。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen at Renshou Palace was about to die, the Crown Prince and Yang Su forged an edict ordering Yan and Yuwen Shu to lead the Eastern Palace troops, post them to guard the upper terrace overnight, and put gate control entirely in their hands.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen lay dying at Renshou Palace, the crown prince and Yang Su forged an edict placing Yan and Yuwen Shu in command of the eastern palace troops to guard the palace gates and terraces.

sentences.zh: 及上崩，漢王起逆，而京師空虛，使衍馳還，總兵居守。

translations.literal: When the sovereign died, the Prince of Han raised rebellion while the capital was empty; Yan was sent galloping back to gather troops and hold the defense.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor died, the Prince of Han rebelled while the capital was undefended; Yan was sent galloping back to gather troops and hold the city.

sentences.zh: 大業元年，拜左武衛大將軍。

translations.literal: In the first year of Daye, he was appointed Grand General of the Left Martial Guard.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Daye, he was appointed grand general of the left martial guard.

sentences.zh: 帝幸江都，令統左軍，改授光祿大夫，又從征吐谷渾，出金山道，納降二萬餘戶。

translations.literal: The emperor visited Jiangdu, ordered him to command the left army, changed his appointment to grand master of splendid happiness, and again followed the campaign against Tuyuhun, taking the Jinshan route and accepting the surrender of more than twenty thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor visited Jiangdu, ordered him to take command of the left army, transferred him to grand master of splendid happiness, and again followed the campaign against Tuyuhun; marching by the Jinshan route, he accepted the surrender of more than twenty thousand households.

sentences.zh: 衍能揣上意，阿諛順旨，帝每謂人曰：「唯郭衍心與朕同。」

translations.literal: Yan could gauge the sovereign's intent and flatter to comply with his wishes; the emperor often told people, "Only Guo Yan's heart is one with mine."
translations.idiomatic: Yan could gauge the emperor's intent and flatter to comply with his wishes; the emperor often told people, "Only Guo Yan's heart is one with mine."

sentences.zh: 又嘗勸帝取樂，五日一視事，無得效高祖空自劬勞。

translations.literal: He also once urged the emperor to take his pleasures, attend to affairs once every five days, and not imitate Emperor Wen in wearing himself out to no purpose.
translations.idiomatic: He also once urged the emperor to take his ease, attend to affairs only once every five days, and not imitate Emperor Wen in wearing himself out to no purpose.

sentences.zh: 帝從之，益稱其孝順。

translations.literal: The emperor followed this advice and praised him all the more for filial obedience.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor followed this advice and praised him all the more for filial obedience.

sentences.zh: 初，新令行，衍封爵從例除。

translations.literal: At first, when the new statutes took effect, Yan's enfeoffment and rank were removed according to regulation.
translations.idiomatic: When the new statutes first took effect, Yan's title and enfeoffment were removed according to regulation.

sentences.zh: 六年，以恩舊封真定侯。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, because of old ties of favor he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Zhending.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year, because of old ties of favor he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Zhending.

sentences.zh: 從往江都，卒。

translations.literal: He followed the emperor to Jiangdu and died there.
translations.idiomatic: He followed the emperor to Jiangdu and died there.

sentences.zh: 贈左衛大將軍。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted the title Grand General of the Left Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made grand general of the left guard.

sentences.zh: 諡曰襄。

translations.literal: His posthumous title was Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: His posthumous title was Xiang.

sentences.zh: 長子臻，武牙郎將。

translations.literal: His eldest son Zhen was Commandant of the Martial Fangs.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Zhen was commandant of the martial fangs.

sentences.zh: 次子嗣本，孝昌令。

translations.literal: His second son Siben was Magistrate of Xiaochang.
translations.idiomatic: His second son Siben was magistrate of Xiaochang.

sentences.zh: 張衡，字建平，河內人也。

translations.literal: Zhang Heng, styled Jianping, was a native of Henei.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Heng, courtesy name Jianping, came from Henei commandery.

sentences.zh: 祖嶷，魏河陽太守。

translations.literal: His grandfather Ni was Governor of Heyang in Wei.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Ni had been governor of Heyang under Wei.

sentences.zh: 父允，周萬州刺史。

translations.literal: His father Yun was Governor of Wanzhou under Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yun had served Zhou as governor of Wan province.

sentences.zh: 衡幼懷志尚，有骨梗風。

translations.literal: Heng in youth cherished lofty aims and had a stern, unyielding bearing.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Heng held high ambitions and an unyielding character.

sentences.zh: 十五，詣太學受業，研精覃思，為同輩所推。

translations.literal: At fifteen he went to the Imperial Academy to pursue his studies, penetrating deeply and thinking broadly, and was esteemed by his peers.
translations.idiomatic: At fifteen he entered the Imperial Academy, studied with deep concentration, and was esteemed by his peers.

sentences.zh: 周武帝居太后憂，與左右出獵，衡露髻輿櫬，扣馬切諫。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu of Zhou was in mourning for the Empress Dowager and went out hunting with his attendants, Heng with hair loose carried a bier on his shoulder, seized the horse's bridle, and remonstrated urgently.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu was in mourning for the empress dowager yet went hunting with his attendants, Heng came with hair unbound, carrying a bier on his shoulder, seized the bridle, and remonstrated sharply.

sentences.zh: 帝嘉焉，賜衣一襲，馬一匹，擢拜漢王侍讀。

translations.literal: The Emperor approved, granted him one suit of clothes and one horse, and promoted him to Reader Attendant to the Prince of Han.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved, gave him a suit of clothes and a horse, and made him reader attendant to the Prince of Han.

sentences.zh: 衡又就沈重受《三禮》，略究大旨。

translations.literal: Heng also studied the 《Three Rites》 under Shen Chong and gained some grasp of their main purport.
translations.idiomatic: Heng also studied the 《Three Rites》 under Shen Chong and gained a grasp of their essentials.

sentences.zh: 累遷掌朝大夫。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Grand Master in Charge of the Court.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to grand master in charge of the court.

sentences.zh: 隋文帝受禪，拜司門侍郎。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen of Sui received the abdication, Heng was appointed Vice Director of the Department of Gates.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen took the throne, Heng was made vice director of the department of gates.

sentences.zh: 及晉王廣為河北行台，衡曆刑部、度支二曹郎。

translations.literal: When Prince Jin Guang was made Hebei Executive Abode, Heng successively served as Gentleman of the Bureaus of Punishments and of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Jin Yang Guang was made executive abode of Hebei, Heng served in the bureaus of punishments and of revenue.

sentences.zh: 行台廢，拜并州總管掾。

translations.literal: When the executive abode was abolished, he was appointed aide to the governor-general of Bing province.
translations.idiomatic: When the executive abode was abolished, he was appointed aide to the governor-general of Bing province.

sentences.zh: 王轉牧揚州，衡復為掾。

translations.literal: When the prince transferred his governorship to Yang province, Heng again served as an aide.
translations.idiomatic: When the prince transferred his governorship to Yang province, Heng again served as his aide.

sentences.zh: 王甚親任之，衡亦竭慮盡誠。

translations.literal: The prince was very intimate in employing him, and Heng too exhausted his mind in utmost loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: The prince held him in great favor and trust, and Heng in turn gave his mind and loyalty without reserve.

sentences.zh: 奪宗之計，多衡所建。

translations.literal: Plans to seize the succession — many were Heng's proposals.
translations.idiomatic: Many of the plans to seize the succession were Heng's proposals.

sentences.zh: 遷揚州總管司馬。

translations.literal: He was promoted to chief commandant of the Yangzhou governor-general's headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to chief commandant of the Yangzhou governor-general's headquarters.

sentences.zh: 熙州李英林反，署置百官，以衡為行軍總管討平之，拜開府。

translations.literal: Li Yinglin of Xizhou rebelled, established the hundred officials, and made Heng marching commander-general; he pacified them and was appointed to the Opening Office.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yinglin of Xizhou rebelled, set up a full bureaucracy, and appointed Heng marching commander-general; Heng suppressed the revolt and was then appointed to the Opening Office.

sentences.zh: 及王為皇太子，拜衡右庶子。

translations.literal: When the prince became crown prince, Heng was appointed his right chief supporter.
translations.idiomatic: When the prince became crown prince, Heng was made his right chief supporter.

sentences.zh: 煬帝嗣位，除給事黃門侍郎、銀青光祿大夫。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yang succeeded to the throne, Heng was made attendant of the Yellow Gate Department and Lustered Grand Master of the Palace.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yang succeeded to the throne, Heng was made attendant of the Yellow Gate Department and lustered grand master of the palace.

sentences.zh: 遷御史大夫，甚見親重。

translations.literal: He was promoted to censor-in-chief and was greatly favored and esteemed.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to censor-in-chief and was greatly favored and esteemed.

sentences.zh: 大業三年，帝幸榆林郡，還至太原，謂衡曰：「朕欲過公宅，可為朕作主人也。」

translations.literal: In the third year of Daye, the emperor visited Yunlin commandery; on returning to Taiyuan he said to Heng, "I wish to pass your residence — you can play host for me."
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Daye, the emperor visited Yunlin commandery; on returning to Taiyuan he said to Heng, "I wish to visit your home — you can play host for me."

sentences.zh: 衡馳至河內，與宗族具牛酒。

translations.literal: Heng raced to Henei and with his clan prepared cattle and wine.
translations.idiomatic: Heng raced to Henei and, with his clan, prepared cattle and wine.

sentences.zh: 帝上太行，開直道九十里，以抵其宅。

translations.literal: The emperor ascended the Taihang, opened a direct road of ninety li, and reached his residence.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor crossed the Taihang range, opened a straight road ninety li long, and reached his house.

sentences.zh: 帝悅其山泉，留宴三日，因謂衡曰：「往從先皇拜太山之始，途經洛陽，瞻望於此，深恨不得相過，不謂今日得諧宿願。」

translations.literal: The emperor delighted in his mountain streams, lingered in banquet three days, and said to Heng, "When I formerly followed my late father at the beginning of paying homage at Mount Tai, on the road passing Luoyang I gazed toward this place and deeply regretted that I could not visit you; I never expected today to fulfil that long-held wish."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor delighted in his mountain streams, lingered three days for a banquet, and said to Heng, "When I once followed my late father on the journey to pay homage at Mount Tai, passing through Luoyang I looked toward this place and deeply regretted that I could not visit you — I never expected today to fulfil that long-held wish."

sentences.zh: 衡俯伏辭謝，奉觴上壽。

translations.literal: Heng prostrated himself in thanks and raised a cup to wish him long life.
translations.idiomatic: Heng prostrated himself in thanks and raised a cup to wish him long life.

sentences.zh: 帝益歡，賜其宅傍田三十頃、良馬一匹、金帶、縑彩六百段、衣一襲、禦食器一具。

translations.literal: The emperor grew still more merry and bestowed upon him thirty qing of good fields beside his residence, one fine horse, a gold belt, six hundred lengths of silk brocade, one suit of clothes, and one set of imperial dining vessels.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor grew still more merry and bestowed on him thirty qing of good fields beside his residence, a fine horse, a gold belt, six hundred lengths of silk brocade, a suit of clothes, and a set of imperial dining vessels.

sentences.zh: 衡固讓，帝曰：「天子所至稱幸者，蓋為此也，不足為辭。」

translations.literal: Heng firmly declined; the emperor said, "Wherever the Son of Heaven arrives and calls it a visitation, it is for this — do not decline excessively."
translations.idiomatic: Heng firmly declined; the emperor said, "Wherever the Son of Heaven arrives and calls it a visitation, it is for this — do not decline."

sentences.zh: 衡復獻食於帝，帝令頒賜公卿，下至衛士，無不沾給。

translations.literal: Heng again presented food to the emperor; the emperor ordered it distributed to the public ministers down to the guardsmen — none went without a share.
translations.idiomatic: Heng again presented food to the emperor; the emperor ordered it distributed to the public ministers down to the guardsmen, and none went without a share.

sentences.zh: 衡以籓邸之舊，恩寵莫與為比，頗自驕貴。

translations.literal: Because of his old ties from the prince's establishment, his favor and distinction were unmatched; he became quite proud and self-important.
translations.idiomatic: Because of his old ties from the prince's establishment, his favor and distinction were unmatched, and he grew quite proud and self-important.

sentences.zh: 明年，帝幸汾陽宮。

translations.literal: The next year the emperor visited the Fenyang Palace.
translations.idiomatic: The next year the emperor visited the Fenyang Palace.

sentences.zh: 時帝欲大汾陽宮，令衡與紀弘整具圖奏之。

translations.literal: At that time the emperor wished to enlarge the Fenyang Palace and ordered Heng and Ji Hongzheng to draw up plans and present them.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the emperor wished to enlarge the Fenyang Palace and ordered Heng and Ji Hongzheng to prepare plans and present them.

sentences.zh: 衡承間進諫，以比年勞役，百姓疲敝為請。

translations.literal: Heng seized an opportune moment to remonstrate, pleading on behalf of the people worn out by labor levies in recent years.
translations.idiomatic: Heng seized an opportune moment to remonstrate, pleading on behalf of the people worn out by labor levies in recent years.

sentences.zh: 帝意甚不平。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly displeased in mind.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was greatly displeased.

sentences.zh: 後嘗目衡謂侍臣曰：「張衡自謂由甚計畫，令我有天下。」

translations.literal: Later the emperor looked at Heng and said to his attendants, "Zhang Heng claims that through his schemes he has given me the empire."
translations.idiomatic: Later the emperor looked at Heng and said to his attendants, "Zhang Heng claims that through his schemes he has given me the empire."

sentences.zh: 時齊王暕失愛於上，帝密令人求其罪。

translations.literal: At that time the Prince of Qi Yang Yong had lost the emperor's favor; the emperor secretly had people seek his faults.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Prince of Qi Yang Yong had lost the emperor's favor, and the emperor secretly had people seek his faults.

sentences.zh: 有人譖暕違制，將伊闕令皇甫詡從之汾陽宮。

translations.literal: Someone slandered Yong for violating regulations in taking Huangfu Xu, magistrate of Yique, with him to the Fenyang Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Someone slandered Yong for violating regulations in taking Huangfu Xu, magistrate of Yique, with him to the Fenyang Palace.

sentences.zh: 又錄前幸涿郡及祠恆岳時，父老謁見者，衣冠不整。

translations.literal: He also recorded that when the emperor had formerly visited Zhuo commandery and sacrificed at Mount Heng, the elders who came to audience were not properly dressed.
translations.idiomatic: He also recorded that on the emperor's earlier visits to Zhuo commandery and his sacrifice at Mount Heng, the elders who came to audience were not properly dressed.

sentences.zh: 帝譴衡以憲司皆不能舉正，出為榆林太守。

translations.literal: The emperor blamed Heng because the censorate officials could not impeach and correct these matters, and sent him out as governor of Yulin.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor blamed Heng because the censorate officials could not impeach and correct these matters, and sent him out as governor of Yulin.

sentences.zh: 明年，帝復幸汾陽宮，衡督役築樓煩城，因而謁帝。

translations.literal: The next year the emperor again visited the Fenyang Palace; Heng supervised labor building Loufan city and thereupon had audience with the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: The next year the emperor again visited the Fenyang Palace; Heng supervised labor on Loufan city and thereupon had audience with the emperor.

sentences.zh: 帝惡衡不損瘦，以為不念咎，因謂曰：「公甚肥澤，宜且還郡。」

translations.literal: The emperor disliked that Heng had not grown lean and took it that he did not dwell on his fault; he therefore said, "You are quite fat and sleek — you had better return to your commandery for now."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor disliked that Heng had not grown lean and took it that he did not dwell on his fault; he therefore said, "You are quite fat and sleek — you had better return to your commandery for now."

sentences.zh: 衡復之榆林。

translations.literal: Heng returned to Yulin.
translations.idiomatic: Heng returned to Yulin.

sentences.zh: 俄而敕衡督役江都宮。

translations.literal: Soon an edict ordered Heng to supervise work on the Jiangdu Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Soon an edict ordered Heng to supervise work on the Jiangdu Palace.

sentences.zh: 有人詣衡訟宮監者，衡不為理，還以訟書付監，其人大為監所困。

translations.literal: Someone came to Heng to sue the palace overseer; Heng would not hear the case and instead returned the petition to the overseer, and the man was greatly harassed by the overseer.
translations.idiomatic: Someone came to Heng to sue the palace overseer; Heng would not hear the case and instead returned the petition to the overseer, and the man was greatly harassed by the overseer.

sentences.zh: 禮部尚書楊玄感使至江都，其人詣玄感稱冤。

translations.literal: Minister of Rites Yang Xuangan sent an envoy to Jiangdu; the man went to Xuangan to proclaim his grievance.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Rites Yang Xuangan sent an envoy to Jiangdu; the man went to Xuangan to proclaim his grievance.

sentences.zh: 玄感固以衡為不可。」

translations.literal: Xuangan firmly maintained that Heng was unacceptable.
translations.idiomatic: Xuangan firmly maintained that Heng was unacceptable.

sentences.zh: 及與相見，未有所言，又先謂玄感曰：「薛道衡真為枉死。」

translations.literal: When they met, before anything was said, he first said to Xuangan, "Xue Daohang truly died a wrongful death."
translations.idiomatic: When they met, before anything was said, he first said to Xuangan, "Xue Daohang truly died a wrongful death."

sentences.zh: 玄感具上其事。

translations.literal: Xuangan reported the whole affair in full to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Xuangan reported the whole affair in full to the throne.

sentences.zh: 江都郡丞王世充又奏衡頻減頓具。

translations.literal: Wang Shichong, deputy magistrate of Jiangdu commandery, also memorialized that Heng repeatedly cut back provisions and equipment.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shichong, deputy magistrate of Jiangdu commandery, also memorialized that Heng repeatedly cut back provisions and equipment.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，鎖衡詣江都市，將斬之。

translations.literal: The emperor was furious, chained Heng, and sent him to Jiangdu city to be executed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was furious, chained Heng, and sent him to Jiangdu city to be executed.

sentences.zh: 既而除名，放還田里。

translations.literal: Shortly thereafter his name was removed from the registers and he was released to return to his home village.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly thereafter his name was removed from the registers and he was released to return to his home village.

sentences.zh: 帝每令親人覘衡所為。

translations.literal: The emperor often had his kin spy on what Heng was doing.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor often had his kin spy on what Heng was doing.

sentences.zh: 八年，帝自遼東還都，妄言衡怨望，謗訕朝政，帝賜死於家。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, when the emperor returned from Liaodong to the capital, he falsely claimed that Heng resented and slandered the government; the emperor had him put to death at home.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year, when the emperor returned from Liaodong to the capital, he falsely claimed that Heng resented and slandered the government, and the emperor had him put to death at home.

sentences.zh: 臨死，大言曰：「我為人作何物事，而望久活！」

translations.literal: As he faced death he cried out loudly, "What sort of man's work have I done, that I should hope to live long!"
translations.idiomatic: As he faced death he cried out loudly, "What sort of man's work have I done, that I should hope to live long!"

sentences.zh: 監刑者塞耳，促令殺之。

translations.literal: The supervising executioner stopped his ears and urged that he be killed at once.
translations.idiomatic: The supervising executioner stopped his ears and urged that he be killed at once.

sentences.zh: 武德初，以為死非其罪，贈大將軍、南陽郡公，諡曰忠。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Wude era, it was held that his death was not his crime; he was posthumously made Grand General and Duke of Nanyang, with posthumous title Zhong.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Wude era, it was held that his death was not his crime; he was posthumously made grand general and Duke of Nanyang, with posthumous title Zhong.

sentences.zh: 子希玄。

translations.literal: His son was Xi Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Xi Xuan.

sentences.zh: 楊汪，字元度，本弘農華陰人也。

translations.literal: Yang Wang, styled Yuandu, was originally a native of Huayin in Hongnong.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Wang, courtesy name Yuandu, was originally from Huayin in Hongnong.

sentences.zh: 曾祖順，居河東。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Shun lived in Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Shun lived in Hedong.

sentences.zh: 父琛，儀同三司。

translations.literal: His father Chen was Palace Attendant of the Third Rank.
translations.idiomatic: His father Chen was palace attendant of the third rank.

sentences.zh: 及汪貴，追贈平鄉縣公。

translations.literal: When Wang rose to prominence, [his ancestors] were posthumously enfeoffed as Duke of Pingxiang county.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang rose to prominence, his forebears were posthumously enfeoffed as Duke of Pingxiang county.

sentences.zh: 汪少凶疏，與人群鬥，拳所毆擊，無不顛踣。

translations.literal: In youth Wang was violent and undisciplined; when he fought in crowds, none struck by his fists failed to topple over.
translations.idiomatic: In youth Wang was violent and undisciplined; in brawls none struck by his fists failed to topple.

sentences.zh: 長更折節勤學，專精《左氏傳》，通《三禮》。

translations.literal: When he grew older he reformed his conduct and studied diligently, specializing in the 《Left Tradition》 and mastering the 《Three Rites》.
translations.idiomatic: When he grew older he reformed his conduct and studied diligently, specializing in the 《Left Tradition》 and mastering the 《Three Rites》.

sentences.zh: 解褐周冀王侍讀，王甚重之，每曰：「楊侍讀德業優深，孤之穆生也。」

translations.literal: On leaving the gray, he was reader to the Prince of Ji of Zhou; the prince greatly esteemed him and often said, "Reader Yang's virtue and learning are outstanding in depth — he is my Mushang!"
translations.idiomatic: On leaving the gray, he was reader to the Prince of Ji of Zhou; the prince greatly esteemed him and often said, "Reader Yang's virtue and learning are profound — he is my Mushang!"

sentences.zh: 後問《禮》於沈重，受《漢書》于劉臻，二人曰：「吾弗如也。」

translations.literal: Later he studied the 《Rites》 under Shen Chong and received the 《Book of Han》 from Liu Zhen; both men said, "We are not his equal."
translations.idiomatic: Later he studied the 《Rites》 under Shen Chong and received the 《Book of Han》 from Liu Zhen; both men said, "We are not his equal."

sentences.zh: 由是知名。

translations.literal: Thereby he became renowned.
translations.idiomatic: Thereby he became renowned.

sentences.zh: 累遷夏官府都上士。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to chief officer of the Xia Offices in the palace directorate.
translations.idiomatic: He was repeatedly promoted to chief officer of the Xia Offices in the palace directorate.

sentences.zh: 隋文帝居相，引知兵事，遷掌朝下大夫。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen of Sui was in charge at Xiang, he drew Wang in to know military affairs and promoted him to grand master in charge of the court.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen of Sui was regent at Xiang, he drew Wang in to know military affairs and promoted him to grand master in charge of the court.

sentences.zh: 及受禪，賜爵平鄉縣伯，曆秦州總管府長史。

translations.literal: When he received the abdication, Wang was granted the title of Earl of Pingxiang county and served as chief clerk of the Qinzhou governor-general's headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: When he received the abdication, Wang was granted the title of Earl of Pingxiang county and served as chief clerk of the Qinzhou governor-general's headquarters.

sentences.zh: 每聽政暇，必延生徒講授，時人稱之。

translations.literal: Whenever he had leisure after hearing cases, he would always invite students to lecture; people of the time praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he had leisure after hearing cases, he would always invite students to lecture, and people of the time praised him.

sentences.zh: 入為尚書兵部侍郎。

translations.literal: He entered court as vice minister of the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: He entered court as vice minister of the Ministry of War.

sentences.zh: 數年，帝謂諫議大夫王達曰：「卿為我覓一好左丞。」

translations.literal: After several years the emperor said to Remonstrating Grand Master Wang Da, "Find me a good left vice minister."
translations.idiomatic: After several years the emperor said to remonstrating grand master Wang Da, "Find me a good left vice minister."

sentences.zh: 達遂私于汪曰：「我當薦君為左丞，若事果，當以良田相報也。」
