translations.literal: Da then privately told Wang, "I intend to recommend you as left vice minister; if it succeeds, I shall repay you with good fields."
translations.idiomatic: Da then privately told Wang, "I intend to recommend you as left vice minister; if it succeeds, I shall repay you with good fields."

sentences.zh: 汪以達言奏之，達竟獲罪，卒拜汪尚書左丞。

translations.literal: Wang reported Da's words to the throne; Da ended up being punished, and Wang was at last appointed Left Vice Minister of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: Wang reported Da's words to the throne; Da ended up being punished, and Wang was at last appointed left vice minister of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 汪明習法令，果於剖斷，當時號為稱職。

translations.literal: Wang was well versed in statutes and decisive in judgment; he was at the time acclaimed as competent in office.
translations.idiomatic: Wang was well versed in statutes and decisive in judgment; at the time he was acclaimed as competent in office.

sentences.zh: 未幾，坐事免。

translations.literal: Before long he was dismissed on account of an offense.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was dismissed on account of an offense.

sentences.zh: 後拜洛州長史，轉荊州長史。

translations.literal: Later he was appointed chief magistrate of Luozhou, then transferred to chief magistrate of Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was appointed chief magistrate of Luozhou, then transferred to chief magistrate of Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 煬帝即位，追為尚書左丞，尋守大理卿。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yang took the throne, Wang was recalled as Left Vice Minister of the Masters of Writing and soon served as acting minister of justice.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yang took the throne, Wang was recalled as left vice minister of the Masters of Writing and soon served as acting minister of justice.

sentences.zh: 視事二日，帝將親省囚徒。

translations.literal: After two days in office the emperor was going personally to review the prisoners.
translations.idiomatic: After two days in office the emperor was going personally to review the prisoners.

sentences.zh: 時系囚二百餘人，汪通宵究審，詰朝而奏，曲盡事情，一無遺誤，帝甚嘉之。

translations.literal: At the time more than two hundred prisoners were held; Wang examined them through the night, reported at dawn, and set forth the cases fully with not a single error; the emperor greatly approved.
translations.idiomatic: At the time more than two hundred prisoners were held; Wang examined them through the night, reported at dawn, and set forth the cases fully without a single error; the emperor greatly approved.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，拜國子祭酒。

translations.literal: After more than a year he was appointed director of the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: After more than a year he was appointed director of the Imperial Academy.

sentences.zh: 帝令百僚就學，與汪講論。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered the hundred officials to attend study and debate with Wang.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered the hundred officials to attend study and debate with Wang.

sentences.zh: 天下通儒碩學多萃焉，論難鋒起，皆不能屈。

translations.literal: The empire's leading Confucians and great scholars largely gathered there; challenges flew thick and fast, yet none could overcome him.
translations.idiomatic: The empire's leading Confucians and great scholars largely gathered there; challenges flew thick and fast, yet none could overcome him.

sentences.zh: 帝令御史書其問答奏之，省而大悅，賜良馬一匹。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered the censor to record their questions and answers and present them; he read them with great delight and bestowed one fine horse.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered the censor to record their questions and answers and present them; he read them with great delight and bestowed a fine horse.

sentences.zh: 後加銀青光祿大夫。

translations.literal: Later he was advanced to Lustered Grand Master of the Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was advanced to lustered grand master of the palace.

sentences.zh: 及楊玄感反，河南贊務裴弘策出師禦之，戰不利，奔還，遇汪而屏人交語。

translations.literal: When Yang Xuangan rebelled, Coordinator of Henan Pei Hongce went out with troops to resist; the fight went badly and he fled back, met Wang, and dismissed others to speak with him privately.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Xuangan rebelled, coordinator of Henan Pei Hongce went out with troops to resist; the fight went badly and he fled back, met Wang, and dismissed others to speak with him privately.

sentences.zh: 既而留守樊子蓋斬弘策，以狀奏汪，帝疑之，出為梁郡通守。

translations.literal: Then the garrison commander Fan Zigai executed Hongce and memorialized the facts regarding Wang; the emperor was suspicious and sent Wang out as communications commissioner of Liang commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Then the garrison commander Fan Zigai executed Hongce and memorialized the facts regarding Wang; the emperor was suspicious and sent Wang out as communications commissioner of Liang commandery.

sentences.zh: 後煬帝崩，王世充推越王侗為主，徵拜吏部尚書，頗見親委。

translations.literal: Later, when Emperor Yang died, Wang Shichong installed the Prince of Yue Yang Tong as ruler, summoned Wang as Minister of Personnel, and greatly trusted him.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when Emperor Yang died, Wang Shichong installed the Prince of Yue Yang Tong as ruler, summoned Wang as minister of personnel, and greatly trusted him.

sentences.zh: 及世充僭號，汪復用事。

translations.literal: When Shichong usurped the throne, Wang again held power.
translations.idiomatic: When Shichong usurped the throne, Wang again held power.

sentences.zh: 世充平，遂以凶黨伏誅。

translations.literal: When Shichong was overthrown, Wang was executed as a member of the evil faction.
translations.idiomatic: When Shichong was overthrown, Wang was executed as a member of the evil faction.

sentences.zh: 裴蘊，河東聞喜人也。

translations.literal: Pei Yun was a native of Wenxi in Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Yun was from Wenxi in Hedong.

sentences.zh: 祖之平，父忌，並《南史》有傳。

translations.literal: His grandfather Zhiping and his father Ji both have biographies in the 《Records of the Southern Dynasties》.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Zhiping and his father Ji both have biographies in the 《Records of the Southern Dynasties》.

sentences.zh: 忌在陳，與吳明徹同見俘于周，周賜爵江夏公，在隋十餘年而卒。

translations.literal: Ji was in Chen; he and Wu Mingche were captured together by Zhou; Zhou enfeoffed him as Duke of Jiangxia; he died after more than ten years in Sui.
translations.idiomatic: Ji was in Chen; he and Wu Mingche were captured together by Zhou; Zhou enfeoffed him as Duke of Jiangxia, and he died after more than ten years in Sui.

sentences.zh: 蘊明辯有吏幹，仕陳，曆直閣將軍、興甯令。

translations.literal: Yun was bright in debate and skilled in administrative affairs; he served Chen as General of the Direct Office, magistrate of Xingning.
translations.idiomatic: Yun was bright in debate and skilled in administrative affairs; he served Chen as general of the direct office and magistrate of Xingning.

sentences.zh: 以父在北，陰奉表于隋文帝，請為內應。

translations.literal: Because his father was in the north, he secretly submitted a memorial to Emperor Wen of Sui asking to serve as inner collaborator.
translations.idiomatic: Because his father was in the north, he secretly submitted a memorial to Emperor Wen of Sui asking to serve as an inside collaborator.

sentences.zh: 及陳平，上悉閱江南衣冠之士，次至蘊，以夙有向化心，超授儀同。

translations.literal: When Chen was pacified, the emperor reviewed the cap-and-gown scholars of the south in turn; when it came to Yun, because he had long had a heart turned toward transformation, he was exceptionally appointed Palace Attendant of the First Rank.
translations.idiomatic: When Chen was pacified, the emperor reviewed the cap-and-gown scholars of the south in turn; when it came to Yun, because he had long had a heart set on coming over to Sui, he was exceptionally appointed palace attendant of the first rank.

sentences.zh: 僕射高熲不悟上旨，諫曰：「蘊無功于國，寵逾倫輩，臣未見其可。」

translations.literal: Vice Director Gao Jiong did not grasp the emperor's intent and remonstrated, "Yun has no merit to the state; his favor exceeds his rank; I do not see how this is acceptable."
translations.idiomatic: Vice director Gao Jiong did not grasp the emperor's intent and remonstrated, "Yun has no merit to the state; his favor exceeds his rank — I do not see how this is acceptable."

sentences.zh: 又加上儀同，復諫。

translations.literal: [The emperor] again added Senior Palace Attendant of the First Rank; [Gao] again remonstrated.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor again added senior palace attendant of the first rank, and Gao again remonstrated.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「可加開府。」

translations.literal: The emperor said, "He may be made Opening Office."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "He may be made Opening Office."

sentences.zh: 乃不敢復言。

translations.literal: Thereupon he did not dare speak again.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he did not dare speak again.

sentences.zh: 即日拜開府儀同三司，禮賜優洽。

translations.literal: That very day Yun was appointed Palace Attendant of the First Rank with the Opening Office, with ritual courtesies and gifts liberal and appropriate.
translations.idiomatic: That very day Yun was appointed palace attendant of the first rank with the opening office, with ritual courtesies and gifts liberal and appropriate.

sentences.zh: 曆洋、直隸三州刺史，俱有能名。

translations.literal: He served successively as governor of Yang, Zhili, and San provinces, all with a reputation for ability.
translations.idiomatic: He served successively as governor of Yang, Zhili, and San provinces, all with a reputation for ability.

sentences.zh: 大業初，考績連最。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Daye, his merit evaluations were consecutively the highest.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Daye, his merit evaluations were consecutively the highest.

sentences.zh: 煬帝聞其善政，徵為太常少卿。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yang heard of his good governance, he summoned him as vice minister of court ceremonials.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yang heard of his good governance, he summoned him as vice minister of court ceremonials.

sentences.zh: 初，文帝不好聲技，遣牛弘定樂，非正聲清商及九部四舞之色，皆罷遣從百姓。

translations.literal: Initially Emperor Wen did not favor musical arts; he had Niu Hong fix the music, and nonstandard tones, clear shang, and the colors of the nine departments and four dances were all dismissed to return to commoners.
translations.idiomatic: Initially Emperor Wen did not favor musical arts; he had Niu Hong fix the music, and nonstandard tones, clear shang, and the colors of the nine departments and four dances were all dismissed to return to commoners.

sentences.zh: 至是，蘊揣知帝意，奏括天下周、齊、梁、陳樂家子弟，皆為樂戶。

translations.literal: By then Yun guessed the emperor's mind and memorialized to round up the sons and younger brothers of musician families throughout the empire from Zhou, Qi, Liang, and Chen — all were made music households.
translations.idiomatic: By then Yun guessed the emperor's mind and memorialized to round up the sons and younger brothers of musician families throughout the empire from Zhou, Qi, Liang, and Chen, and all were made music households.

sentences.zh: 其六品已下，至於凡庶，有善音樂及倡優百戲者，皆直太常。

translations.literal: From the sixth rank down to commoners, anyone skilled in music or in performers and hundred entertainments was all assigned straight to the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: From the sixth rank down to commoners, anyone skilled in music or in performers and hundred entertainments was all assigned straight to the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 是後異技淫聲咸萃樂府，皆置博士，遞相教傳，增益樂人至三萬餘。

translations.literal: Thereafter exotic arts and licentious sounds all gathered in the Music Office; masters were established in succession to teach one another, and musicians were increased to more than thirty thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter exotic arts and licentious sounds all gathered in the Music Office; masters were established in succession to teach one another, and musicians were increased to more than thirty thousand.

sentences.zh: 帝大悅，遷戶部侍郎。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly pleased and promoted Yun to vice minister of the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was greatly pleased and promoted Yun to vice minister of the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 時猶承文帝和平後，禁網疏闊，戶口多漏。

translations.literal: The times still bore the peace after Emperor Wen, and the prohibition net was slack; many household registrations were omitted.
translations.idiomatic: The times still bore the peace after Emperor Wen, and the prohibition net was slack; many household registrations were omitted.

sentences.zh: 或年及成丁，猶詐為小，未至於老，已免租賦。

translations.literal: Some reached the age of full adulthood yet falsely claimed to be young; before reaching old age they were already exempted from rent and tax.
translations.idiomatic: Some reached the age of full adulthood yet falsely claimed to be young; before reaching old age they were already exempted from rent and tax.

sentences.zh: 蘊曆為刺史，素知其情，因是條奏，皆令貌閱。

translations.literal: Yun had served as governor and long knew these conditions; he therefore memorialized item by item, and all were ordered to undergo physical inspection.
translations.idiomatic: Yun had served as governor and long knew these conditions; he therefore memorialized item by item, and all were ordered to undergo physical inspection.

sentences.zh: 若一人不實，則官司解職，鄉正、里長皆遠流配。

translations.literal: If even one person was not truthful, then the office officials were dismissed from post, and the district head and hamlet chief were all banished to distant penal service.
translations.idiomatic: If even one person was found false, the registering officials lost their posts, and the district head and hamlet chief were all exiled to distant penal service.

sentences.zh: 又許民相告，若糾得一丁者，令被糾之家代輸賦役。

translations.literal: He also permitted the people to inform on one another; if one adult male was seized through denunciation, he ordered the denounced household to pay his taxes and corvée in his stead.
translations.idiomatic: He also allowed the people to inform on one another: if one adult male was turned in, the household denounced had to pay that man's taxes and corvée labor in his place.

sentences.zh: 是歲大業五年也。

translations.literal: That year was the fifth year of Daye.
translations.idiomatic: That year was the fifth year of Daye.

sentences.zh: 諸郡計帳，進丁二十四萬三千，新附口六十四萬一千五百。

translations.literal: The provincial registry accounts reported newly entered adult males of two hundred forty-three thousand and newly attached mouths of six hundred forty-one thousand five hundred.
translations.idiomatic: The provincial registry accounts reported 243,000 newly registered adult males and 641,500 newly attached dependents.

sentences.zh: 帝臨朝覽狀，謂百官曰：「前代無好人，致此罔冒。

translations.literal: The emperor attended court to review the reports and said to the hundred officials: "Former ages had no good men, and this led to such fraud.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor attended court to review the returns and said to the officials: "Former ages had no good men, and that is what led to such fraud.

sentences.zh: 今進民口皆從實者，全由裴蘊一人用心。

translations.literal: Now the registered population submitted is all according to truth — entirely through Pei Yun's single-hearted effort.
translations.idiomatic: Now the population submitted is all truthful — entirely through Pei Yun's devoted effort alone.

sentences.zh: 古語雲，得賢而理，驗之信矣。」

translations.literal: The old saying goes, 'with a worthy man obtained, order follows' — how true it proves."
translations.idiomatic: As the old saying has it, 'obtain a worthy man and the realm is governed' — how true that proves."

sentences.zh: 由是漸見親委，拜京兆贊務，發擿纖毫，吏民懾憚。

translations.literal: Thereupon he was gradually seen in intimate trust, appointed Jingzhao Assistant Commissioner, exposing even the finest threads; officials and commoners alike were in awe.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he was gradually entrusted with intimate duties, appointed assistant commissioner of the capital district, and exposed wrongdoing down to the finest thread; officials and commoners alike were in awe of him.

sentences.zh: 未幾，擢授御史大夫，與裴矩、虞世基參掌機密。

translations.literal: Before long he was promoted and appointed Imperial Censor-in-Chief, and with Pei Ju and Yu Shiji jointly handled secret affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was promoted to imperial censor-in-chief and, together with Pei Ju and Yu Shiji, shared control of confidential state business.

sentences.zh: 蘊善候伺人主微意，若欲罪者，則曲法順情，鍛成其罪；

translations.literal: Yun was skilled at watching for the sovereign's subtle intent; if he wished to punish someone, he would bend the law to suit the mood and forge the crime;
translations.idiomatic: Yun was adept at watching the sovereign's subtle intent: if the emperor wished someone punished, he would bend the law to suit his mood and forge a conviction;

sentences.zh: 所欲宥者，則附從輕典，因而釋之。

translations.literal: if he wished to pardon someone, he would cite lighter statutes and thereby release him.
translations.idiomatic: if the emperor wished someone pardoned, he would cite lighter statutes and thereby set the person free.

sentences.zh: 是後大小之獄皆以付蘊，憲部、大理莫敢與奪，必稟承進止，然後決斷。

translations.literal: Thereafter all great and small cases were entrusted to Yun; the Ministry of Justice and the Court of Judicial Review dared not dispute — they had to await his reporting of instructions before deciding.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter all criminal cases, great and small, were handed to Yun; the Ministry of Justice and the Court of Judicial Review dared not contest his judgments — they had to await his instructions before deciding anything.

sentences.zh: 蘊亦機辯，所論法理，言若懸河，或重或輕，皆由其口，剖析明敏，時人不能致詰。

translations.literal: Yun was also quick in debate; when he argued legal principles his speech was like a hanging river; whether heavy or light, all was by his mouth; his analysis was clear and sharp, and none of the time could pose questions to him.
translations.idiomatic: Yun was also quick-witted in debate: when he argued points of law his speech poured like a hanging river; whether the penalty was heavy or light, all hung on his word. His analysis was lucid and sharp, and no one of the day could cross-examine him.

sentences.zh: 楊玄感之反也，帝遣蘊推其黨與，謂蘊曰：「玄感一呼，從者十萬。

translations.literal: When Yang Xuangan rebelled, the emperor sent Yun to investigate his associates and said to Yun: "With one cry from Xuangan, a hundred thousand followed.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Xuangan rebelled, the emperor sent Yun to investigate his associates and said to him: "Xuangan gave one shout and a hundred thousand men followed him.

sentences.zh: 益知天下人不欲多，多即相聚為盜耳。

translations.literal: This makes it clearer that the people under Heaven do not wish to be numerous — when numerous they simply gather to become bandits.
translations.idiomatic: This only proves that the people under Heaven do not want to be numerous — when they are too numerous they simply gather and become bandits.

sentences.zh: 不盡加誅，則後無以勸。」

translations.literal: If we do not execute them all, afterward there will be no way to encourage obedience."
translations.idiomatic: If we do not put them all to death, afterward there will be no way to enforce obedience."

sentences.zh: 蘊由是乃峻法理之，所戮者數萬人，皆籍沒其家。

translations.literal: Yun therefore rigorously applied the law; those put to death numbered in the tens of thousands, and all their households were confiscated.
translations.idiomatic: Yun therefore applied the law with extreme severity; those executed numbered in the tens of thousands, and all their households were confiscated.

sentences.zh: 帝大稱善，賜奴婢十五口。

translations.literal: The emperor greatly praised this and bestowed fifteen slave households.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised this highly and bestowed fifteen households of slaves.

sentences.zh: 司隸大夫薛道衡以忤意獲譴，蘊知帝惡之，乃奏曰：「道衡負才恃舊，有無君之心。

translations.literal: Supervisor-in-Chief Xue Daoheng was condemned for offending the emperor's wishes; Yun knew the emperor detested him and memorialized: "Daoheng relies on his talent and trusts in old standing; he harbors a heart of disloyalty to his ruler.
translations.idiomatic: Supervisor-in-chief Xue Daoheng was punished for offending the emperor; Yun knew the emperor hated him and memorialized: "Daoheng relies on his talent and his long standing; he harbors a heart that disowns his ruler.

sentences.zh: 見詔書每下，便腹非私議，推惡于國，妄造禍端。

translations.literal: Whenever an edict issues he privately voices discontent, shifts blame onto the state, and recklessly manufactures calamity.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever an edict is issued he privately voices discontent, shifts blame onto the state, and recklessly manufactures disaster.

sentences.zh: 論其罪名，似如隱昧，源其情意，深為悖逆。」

translations.literal: Judged by the name of his crime it seems hidden and obscure; traced to his intent it is deeply rebellious."
translations.idiomatic: Judged by the name of his offense it seems obscure, but traced to his intent it is deeply treasonous."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「然。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "So it is.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "Exactly.

sentences.zh: 我少時與此人相隨行役，輕我童稚，共高熲、賀若弼等外擅威權。

translations.literal: In my youth I served corvée alongside this man; he looked down on me as a child and, together with Gao Jiong, He Ruo Bi, and the like, arrogated power outside.
translations.idiomatic: When I was young I served corvée alongside this man; he looked down on me as a boy and, together with Gao Jiong, He Ruo Bi, and others, arrogated power on the outside.

sentences.zh: 自知罪當誣罔，及我即位，懷不自安，賴天下無事，未得反耳。

translations.literal: He knew his offense deserved denial and deception; when I took the throne he could not feel secure — only because the realm was at peace did he not yet rebel.
translations.idiomatic: He knew his crimes deserved denial and deceit; when I took the throne he could not feel secure — only because the realm was at peace did he not yet rebel.

sentences.zh: 公論其逆。

translations.literal: Your lordship state the case of his rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: State the case of his treason.

sentences.zh: 妙體本心。」

translations.literal: You grasp the heart of the matter beautifully."
translations.idiomatic: You have grasped the heart of the matter beautifully."

sentences.zh: 於是誅道衡。

translations.literal: Thereupon Daoheng was executed.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Daoheng was executed.

sentences.zh: 又帝問蘇威以討遼之策，威不願帝復行，且欲令帝知天下多賊，乃詭答：「今者之役，不願發兵，但詔赦群盜，自可得數十萬。

translations.literal: The emperor also asked Su Wei about strategy against Liaodong; Wei did not wish the emperor to go again and wanted the emperor to know how many bandits there were in the realm, so he answered deceitfully: "For this campaign I would not wish to send troops; merely issue an edict pardoning the bandit hosts and you will yourself obtain several hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor also asked Su Wei about strategy against Liaodong; Wei did not want the emperor to campaign again and wished the emperor to know how many bandits there were in the realm, so he answered deceitfully: "For this campaign I would rather not send troops; merely issue an edict pardoning the bandit hosts and you will yourself obtain several hundred thousand men.

sentences.zh: 遣關內奴賊及山東曆山飛、張金稱等頭別為一軍，出遼西道；

translations.literal: Dispatch the slave bandits within the passes and the Shandong chiefs Lishan Fei, Zhang Jincheng, and others in a separate army by the Liaoxi route;
translations.idiomatic: Dispatch the slave bandits within the passes and the Shandong chiefs Lishan Fei, Zhang Jincheng, and others as a separate army by the Liaoxi route;

sentences.zh: 諸河南賊王薄、孟讓等十餘頭，並給舟楫，浮滄海道。

translations.literal: give boats to the more than ten chiefs of Henan bandits such as Wang Bo and Meng Rang, and send them by the floating route across the Bohai.
translations.idiomatic: give boats to the more than ten Henan bandit chiefs such as Wang Bo and Meng Rang and send them by sea across the Bohai.

sentences.zh: 必喜於免罪，競務立功，一歲之間，可滅高麗矣。」

translations.literal: They will surely rejoice at escaping punishment and vie to establish merit; within one year Koguryŏ can be destroyed."
translations.idiomatic: They will surely rejoice at escaping punishment and compete to win merit; within a year Koguryŏ can be destroyed."

sentences.zh: 帝不懌曰：「我去尚猶未克，鼠竊安能濟乎！」

translations.literal: The emperor, displeased, said: "When I went I still could not conquer them — how could thieving rats accomplish it!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, displeased, said: "When I went I still could not conquer them — how could thieving rats get the job done!"

sentences.zh: 威出後，蘊奏曰：「此大不遜，天下何處有許多賊！」

translations.literal: After Wei left, Yun memorialized: "This is gross insubordination — where under Heaven are there so many bandits!"
translations.idiomatic: After Wei left, Yun memorialized: "This is gross insubordination — where under Heaven are there so many bandits!"

sentences.zh: 帝悟曰：「老革多奸，將賊脅我。

translations.literal: The emperor understood and said: "That old rebel is full of treachery; he would use bandits to threaten me.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor understood and said: "That old rebel is full of treachery — he means to use bandits to threaten me.

sentences.zh: 欲搭其口，但隱忍之，誠極難耐。」

translations.literal: I want to shut his mouth, yet can only bear with it in silence — truly this is almost unbearable."
translations.idiomatic: I want to shut his mouth, yet can only bear with it in silence — truly this is almost unbearable."

sentences.zh: 蘊知上意，遣張行本奏威罪惡，帝付蘊推鞫之，乃處其死。

translations.literal: Yun knew the emperor's mind, sent Zhang Xingben to memorialize on Wei's crimes; the emperor entrusted him to Yun for examination and prosecution, and thus he was sentenced to death.
translations.idiomatic: Yun knew the emperor's mind, sent Zhang Xingben to memorialize Wei's crimes, and the emperor entrusted Wei to Yun for investigation and prosecution; thus he was sentenced to death.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「未忍便殺。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "I cannot yet bring myself to kill him outright."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "I cannot yet bring myself to kill him outright."

sentences.zh: 遂父子及孫三世並除名。

translations.literal: Thereupon father, son, and grandson for three generations were all struck from the registers.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon father, son, and grandson for three generations were all struck from the registers.

sentences.zh: 蘊又欲重己權勢，令虞世基奏罷司隸刺史以下官屬，增置御史百餘人。

translations.literal: Yun again wished to increase his own authority and had Yu Shiji memorialize to abolish the officials below the provincial inspector of the Secretariat Patrol, adding more than a hundred censors.
translations.idiomatic: Yun again wished to increase his own power and had Yu Shiji memorialize to abolish the officials below the provincial inspector of the secretariat patrol, while adding more than a hundred censors.

sentences.zh: 於是引致奸黠，共為朋黨，郡縣有不附者，陰中之。

translations.literal: Thereupon he drew in the crafty and wicked to form factions together; wherever prefectures and counties would not submit, he secretly struck at them.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he drew in the crafty and wicked to form factions; wherever prefectures and counties would not submit, he secretly struck at them.

sentences.zh: 于時軍國多務，凡是興師動眾，京都留守，及與諸蕃互市，皆令御史監之。

translations.literal: At the time military and state affairs were many; whenever troops were raised, when the capital was left on guard, and when trading with the various frontier peoples, censors were all ordered to supervise.
translations.idiomatic: At the time military and state affairs were pressing; whenever troops were raised, when the capital was left under guard, and when trading with the various frontier peoples, censors were ordered to supervise.

sentences.zh: 賓客附隸，遍于郡國，侵擾百姓，帝弗之知也。

translations.literal: Clients and dependents attached to him throughout commanderies and kingdoms, harassing the people — the emperor did not know of it.
translations.idiomatic: Clients and dependents attached to him throughout the commanderies and kingdoms, harassing the people — yet the emperor did not know of it.

sentences.zh: 以度遼之役，進位銀青光祿大夫。

translations.literal: For the campaign across the Liao he was advanced in rank to Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Silver Seal.
translations.idiomatic: For the campaign across the Liao he was promoted to grand master of splendid happiness with silver seal.

sentences.zh: 及司馬德戡將為亂也，江陽長張惠紹夜弛告之。

translations.literal: When Sima Degan was about to raise rebellion, the magistrate of Jiangyang, Zhang Huishao, galloped by night to inform him.
translations.idiomatic: When Sima Degan was about to raise a rebellion, the magistrate of Jiangyang, Zhang Huishao, rode through the night to warn him.

sentences.zh: 蘊共惠紹謀，欲矯詔發郭下兵民，盡取榮公護兒節度，收在外逆党宇文化及等，仍發羽林殿腳，遣范富婁等入自西苑，取梁公蕭钜及燕王處分，扣門援帝。

translations.literal: Yun plotted together with Huishao, wishing to forge an edict to mobilize troops and commoners around the capital, take full command under Duke of Rong Lai Hushen, seize the outside rebel party Yu Wen Huaji and others, also dispatch Palace Guard foot soldiers, send Fan Fulou and others to enter from the Western Park to obtain Duke of Liang Xiao Ju and the Prince of Yan's disposition, break down the gate and rescue the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Yun plotted with Huishao to forge an edict mobilizing troops and commoners around the capital, take full command under Duke of Rong Lai Hushen, seize the outside rebel party led by Yuwen Huaji and others, dispatch Palace Guard foot soldiers, and send Fan Fulou and others in through the Western Park to obtain orders from Duke of Liang Xiao Ju and the Prince of Yan, break down the gate, and rescue the emperor.

sentences.zh: 謀議已定，遣報虞世基。

translations.literal: When the plan was settled he sent word to Yu Shiji.
translations.idiomatic: Once the plan was settled he sent word to Yu Shiji.

sentences.zh: 世基疑反者不實，抑其計。

translations.literal: Shiji doubted the rebels' report was real and suppressed the plan.
translations.idiomatic: Shiji doubted that the report of rebellion was true and suppressed the plan.

sentences.zh: 須臾，難作。

translations.literal: In a moment trouble broke out.
translations.idiomatic: In a moment the crisis broke out.

sentences.zh: 蘊歎曰：「謀及播郎，竟誤人事！」

translations.literal: Yun sighed: "When we consulted Bo-lang — it ruined the affair after all!"
translations.idiomatic: Yun sighed: "When we took counsel with Bo-lang, we ruined the whole affair after all!"

sentences.zh: 遂見害。

translations.literal: Thereupon he was killed.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he was killed.

sentences.zh: 子愔，為尚輦直長，亦同日死。

translations.literal: His son Yin, who served as director of the palace carriage office, died the same day.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yin, who served as director of the palace carriage office, died the same day.

sentences.zh: 袁充，字德符，本陳郡陽夏人也。

translations.literal: Yuan Chong, styled Defu, was originally a native of Yangxia in Chen commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Chong, styled Defu, was originally from Yangxia in Chen commandery.

sentences.zh: 其後寓居丹陽。

translations.literal: Later his family resided in Danyang.
translations.idiomatic: Later his family settled in Danyang.

sentences.zh: 祖昂，父君正，俱為梁侍中。

translations.literal: His grandfather Ang and his father Junzheng both served Liang as Palace Attendants.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Ang and his father Junzheng both served Liang as palace attendants.

sentences.zh: 充少警悟，年十餘歲，其父党至門，時冬初，充尚衣葛衫。

translations.literal: Chong was quick-witted from youth; when he was just over ten, a comrade of his father came to the door — it was early winter and Chong still wore a thin hemp coat.
translations.idiomatic: Chong was quick-witted from childhood; when he was just over ten, a comrade of his father came to the door — it was early winter, yet Chong still wore a thin hemp shirt.

sentences.zh: 客戲充曰：「袁郎子，絺兮綌兮，淒其以風。」

translations.literal: The guest teased Chong: "Young Master Yuan — 'Fine thin cloth, fine coarse cloth — how bitterly the wind cuts!'."
translations.idiomatic: The guest teased him: "Young Master Yuan — 'Fine thin cloth, fine coarse cloth — how bitterly the wind cuts!'."

sentences.zh: 充應聲答曰：「唯絺與綌，服之無斁。」

translations.literal: Chong answered on the spot: "'Only the thin and coarse cloth — wear them and never tire of them.'"
translations.idiomatic: Chong answered on the spot: "'Only the thin cloth and the coarse — wear them and never tire of them.'"

sentences.zh: 以是大見嗟賞。

translations.literal: For this he was greatly praised and admired.
translations.idiomatic: For this he was greatly praised and admired.

sentences.zh: 仕陳，年十七，為秘書郎。

translations.literal: He served Chen; at seventeen he became secretary gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: He served Chen; at seventeen he became a secretary gentleman.

sentences.zh: 曆太子舍人、晉安王文學、吏部侍郎、散騎常侍。

translations.literal: He served successively as crown prince household attendant, literary accoutrement to the Prince of Jin'an, vice director of the Ministry of Personnel, and ordinary attendant-in-attendance.
translations.idiomatic: He served successively as crown prince household attendant, literary accoutrement to the Prince of Jin'an, vice director of the Ministry of Personnel, and ordinary attendant-in-attendance.

sentences.zh: 及陳滅歸國，曆蒙、鄜二州司馬。

translations.literal: When Chen fell he returned to the state and served as military administrator of Meng and Fu prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: When Chen fell he returned to the [Sui] state and served as military administrator of Meng and Fu prefectures.

sentences.zh: 充性好道術，頗解占候，由是領太史令。

translations.literal: Chong was fond of the Way and its arts and understood somewhat of divination and observation; thereby he held the post of Director of the Astronomic Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: Chong was fond of the Way and its arts and understood something of divination and celestial observation; thereby he held the post of director of the astronomic bureau.

sentences.zh: 時上將廢皇太子，正窮東宮官屬，充見上雅信符應，因希旨進曰：「比觀玄象，皇太子當廢。」

translations.literal: The emperor was about to depose the crown prince and was thoroughly investigating the Eastern Palace staff; Chong saw that the emperor deeply trusted omens and portents, and therefore to please him advanced: "I have recently observed the celestial signs — the crown prince ought to be deposed."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was about to depose the crown prince and was thoroughly investigating the Eastern Palace staff; Chong saw that the emperor deeply trusted omens and portents and, to please him, advanced: "I have recently observed the celestial signs — the crown prince ought to be deposed."

sentences.zh: 上然之。

translations.literal: The emperor assented.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor assented.

sentences.zh: 充復表奏隋興以後，日景漸長，曰：「開皇元年，冬至日影一丈二尺七寸二分，自爾漸短。

translations.literal: Chong again memorialized that since the rise of Sui the length of days had gradually increased, saying: "In the first year of Kaihuang, the winter solstice shadow was one zhang, two chi, seven cun, two fen; from then it gradually shortened.
translations.idiomatic: Chong again memorialized that since the rise of Sui the length of days had gradually increased, saying: "In the first year of Kaihuang, the winter solstice shadow was one zhang, two chi, seven cun, and two fen; from then it gradually shortened.

sentences.zh: 至十七年，冬至影一丈二尺六寸三分。

translations.literal: By the seventeenth year the winter solstice shadow was one zhang, two chi, six cun, three fen.
translations.idiomatic: By the seventeenth year the winter solstice shadow was one zhang, two chi, six cun, and three fen.

sentences.zh: 四年冬至，在洛陽測影，一丈二尺八寸八分。

translations.literal: On the fourth year's winter solstice, shadows measured at Luoyang were one zhang, two chi, eight cun, eight fen.
translations.idiomatic: On the fourth year's winter solstice, when shadows were measured at Luoyang, they were one zhang, two chi, eight cun, and eight fen.

sentences.zh: 二年，夏至影一尺四寸八分，自爾漸短。

translations.literal: In the second year the summer solstice shadow was one chi, four cun, eight fen; from then it gradually shortened.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year the summer solstice shadow was one chi, four cun, and eight fen; from then it gradually shortened.

sentences.zh: 至十六年，夏至影一尺四寸五分。

translations.literal: By the sixteenth year the summer solstice shadow was one chi, four cun, five fen.
translations.idiomatic: By the sixteenth year the summer solstice shadow was one chi, four cun, and five fen.

sentences.zh: 《周官》以土圭之法正日影，日至之影尺有五寸。

translations.literal: The 《Rites of Zhou》 uses the earth-sight method to correct the solar shadow; at the solstice the shadow is one chi, five cun.
translations.idiomatic: The 《Rites of Zhou》 uses the earth-sight method to correct the solar shadow; at the solstice the shadow is one chi and five cun.

sentences.zh: 鄭玄云：' 冬至之影一丈三尺。

translations.literal: Zheng Xuan says: 'At the winter solstice the shadow is one zhang, three chi.'
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Xuan says: 'At the winter solstice the shadow is one zhang and three chi.'

sentences.zh: '今十六年夏至之影，短於舊影五分，十七年冬至之影，短於舊影三寸七分。

translations.literal: Now the sixteenth year's summer solstice shadow is five fen shorter than the old shadow; the seventeenth year's winter solstice shadow is three cun, seven fen shorter than the old shadow.
translations.idiomatic: Now the sixteenth year's summer solstice shadow is five fen shorter than the old shadow, and the seventeenth year's winter solstice shadow is three cun and seven fen shorter than the old shadow.

sentences.zh: 日去極近，則影短而日長；

translations.literal: When the sun is near the pole the shadow is short and the day long;
translations.idiomatic: When the sun is near the pole the shadow is short and the day is long;

sentences.zh: 去極遠，則影長而日短。

translations.literal: when far from the pole the shadow is long and the day short.
translations.idiomatic: when it is far from the pole the shadow is long and the day is short.

sentences.zh: 行內道，則去極近；

translations.literal: Traveling the inner path, one is near the pole;
translations.idiomatic: Traveling the inner path, one is near the pole;

sentences.zh: 外道，則去極遠。

translations.literal: the outer path — far from the pole.
translations.idiomatic: the outer path — far from the pole.

sentences.zh: 《堯典》曰：'日短星昴，以正仲冬。

translations.literal: The 《Canon of Yao》 says: 'The days are short and the stars culminate at Mao — thereby the midwinter of the second month is rectified.'
translations.idiomatic: The 《Canon of Yao》 says: 'The days are short and the stars culminate at Mao — thereby the midwinter of the second month is rectified.'

sentences.zh: '據昴星昏中，則知堯時仲冬，日在須女十度。

translations.literal: According to the culmination of Mao at dusk, one knows that at Yao's midwinter the sun was in ten degrees of Maiden.
translations.idiomatic: According to the culmination of Mao at dusk, one knows that at Yao's midwinter the sun was at ten degrees of Maiden.

sentences.zh: 以歷數推之，開皇已來冬至，日在鬥十一度，與唐堯之代，去極並近。

translations.literal: Calculating by the calendar, since Kaihuang the winter solstice sun has been at eleven degrees of Dipper — as in the age of Tang Yao, alike near the pole.
translations.idiomatic: Calculated by the calendar, since Kaihuang the winter solstice sun has been at eleven degrees of Dipper — as in the age of Tang Yao, alike near the pole.

sentences.zh: 謹案《春秋元命包》云：'日月出內道，璿璣得常，天帝崇靈，聖王相功。

translations.literal: Respectfully examining the 《Spring and Autumn Elemental Fate Apocryphon》: it says 'When sun and moon emerge on the inner path, the pivot constant is obtained; the Heavenly Lord honors the numinous; sage kings match merit.'
translations.idiomatic: Respectfully examining the 《Spring and Autumn Elemental Fate Apocryphon》: it says, 'When sun and moon emerge on the inner path, the pivot is kept constant; the Heavenly Lord honors the numinous; sage kings match their merit.'

sentences.zh: '京房《別對》曰：'太平日行上道，升平行次道，霸世行下道。

translations.literal: Jing Fang's 《Separate Responses》 says: 'In great peace the sun travels the upper path; in moderate ascent the middle path; in hegemonic ages the lower path.'
translations.idiomatic: Jing Fang's 《Separate Responses》 says: 'In great peace the sun travels the upper path; in moderate ascent the middle path; in hegemonic ages the lower path.'

sentences.zh: '伏惟大隋啟運，上感乾元，影短日長，振古未之有也。」

translations.literal: Bowing low — great Sui inaugurates its mandate, moved by the primordial heaven — shorter shadows and longer days are something unheard of since antiquity."
translations.idiomatic: Bowing low — great Sui inaugurates its mandate, moved by the primordial heaven — shorter shadows and longer days are something unheard of since antiquity."

sentences.zh: 上大悅，告天下。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly pleased and proclaimed it to all under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was greatly pleased and proclaimed it throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 將作役功，因加程課，丁匠苦之。

translations.literal: The Director of Palace Construction's corvée labor was increased on that account, and the conscript artisans suffered greatly.
translations.idiomatic: The director of palace construction's corvée labor was increased on that account, and the conscript artisans suffered greatly.

sentences.zh: 仁壽初，充言上本命與陰陽律呂合者六十餘條而奏之，因上表曰：「皇帝載誕之初，非止神光瑞氣，嘉祥應感。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Renshou, Chong stated that the emperor's natal destiny matched yin-yang and the pitch-pipes in more than sixty articles and submitted them; he therefore submitted a memorial saying: "At the beginning when the emperor was born, it was not only divine light and auspicious vapors, fortunate signs responding to feeling.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Renshou, Chong stated that the emperor's natal destiny matched yin-yang and the pitch-pipes in more than sixty articles and submitted them; he therefore submitted a memorial saying: "At the hour when the emperor was born, it was not only divine light and auspicious vapors — fortunate signs answered in response.

sentences.zh: 至於本命行年，生月生日，並與天地日月、陰陽律呂，運轉相符，表裏合會。

translations.literal: As for natal year, the year's circuit, birth month, and birth day — all accord with heaven and earth, sun and moon, yin and yang and the pitch-pipes, their revolutions matching inside and out.
translations.idiomatic: As for natal year, the year's circuit, birth month, and birth day — all accord with heaven and earth, sun and moon, yin and yang, and the pitch-pipes; their revolutions match inside and out.

sentences.zh: 此誕聖之異，寶曆之元。

translations.literal: This is the wonder of the sage birth, the origin of the precious succession.
translations.idiomatic: This is the wonder of a sage birth, the origin of a precious succession.

sentences.zh: 今與物更新，改年仁壽，歲月日子，還共誕聖之時並同，明合天地之心，得仁壽之理。

translations.literal: Now, as things renew, the era is changed to Renshou; year, month, day, and child-hour again align with the hour of the sage birth — clearly conforming to heaven and earth's heart and obtaining Renshou's principle.
translations.idiomatic: Now, as things renew, the era is changed to Renshou; year, month, day, and hour again align with the hour of the sage birth — clearly conforming to the heart of heaven and earth and obtaining the principle of Renshou.

sentences.zh: 故知洪基長算，永永無窮。」

translations.literal: Thus one knows the great foundation's long reckoning will endless go on without end."
translations.idiomatic: Thus one knows the great foundation's long reckoning will go on without end."

sentences.zh: 上大悅，賞賜優崇，儕輩莫之比。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly pleased; rewards and favor were exceptional, and none of his peers could compare.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was greatly pleased; rewards and favor were exceptional, and none of his peers could compare.

sentences.zh: 仁壽四年甲子歲，煬帝初即位，充及太史丞高智寶奏言：「去歲冬至，日景逾長。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Renshou, the jiazi year, when Emperor Yang first took the throne, Chong and the deputy director of the astronomic bureau Gao Zhibao submitted: "Last year's winter solstice solar shadow grew yet longer.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Renshou, the jiazi year, when Emperor Yang first took the throne, Chong and the deputy director of the astronomic bureau Gao Zhibao submitted: "Last winter solstice the solar shadow grew yet longer.

sentences.zh: 今歲皇帝即位，與堯受命年合。

translations.literal: This year the emperor ascends the throne, matching the year when Yao received the mandate.
translations.idiomatic: This year the emperor ascends the throne, matching the year when Yao received the mandate.

sentences.zh: 昔唐堯受命四十九年，到上元第一紀甲子，天正十一月庚戍冬至；

translations.literal: Formerly Tang Yao received the mandate in the forty-ninth year, arriving at the jiazi of the first epoch of the upper origin — celestial standard, eleventh month, gengxu, winter solstice;
translations.idiomatic: Formerly Tang Yao received the mandate in the forty-ninth year, arriving at the jiazi of the first epoch of the upper origin — celestial standard, eleventh month, gengxu, winter solstice;

sentences.zh: 陛下即位，其年即當上元第一紀甲子，天正十一月庚戍冬至，正與唐堯同。

translations.literal: when your majesty ascends the throne, that very year is the jiazi of the first epoch of the upper origin — celestial standard, eleventh month, gengxu, winter solstice, exactly as with Tang Yao.
translations.idiomatic: when your majesty ascends the throne, that very year is the jiazi of the first epoch of the upper origin — celestial standard, eleventh month, gengxu, winter solstice, exactly as with Tang Yao.

sentences.zh: 自放勳以來，凡經八上元，其間綿代，未有仁壽甲子之合。

translations.literal: Since the time of Fangxun, eight upper origins have passed in all; through the long dynasties there has never been a Renshou-jiazi conjunction.
translations.idiomatic: Since the time of Fangxun, eight upper origins have passed in all; through the long dynasties there has never been a Renshou-jiazi conjunction.

sentences.zh: 謹案：第一紀甲子，太一在一宮，天目居武德，陰陽曆數，並得符同唐堯。

translations.literal: Respectfully examined: for the jiazi of the first epoch, Great Unity in the first palace, Celestial Eye dwelling in military virtue, yin-yang and calendar numbers all matching Tang Yao.
translations.idiomatic: Respectfully examined: for the jiazi of the first epoch, Great Unity in the first palace, Celestial Eye dwelling in military virtue — yin-yang and calendar numbers all matching Tang Yao.

sentences.zh: 唐堯丙辰生，丙子年受命，止合三五。

translations.literal: Tang Yao was born in bingchen and received the mandate in bingzi, matching only the Three and Five.
translations.idiomatic: Tang Yao was born in bingchen and received the mandate in bingzi, matching only the Three and Five.

sentences.zh: 未若己丑甲子，支干並當六合。

translations.literal: It cannot equal jichou-jiazi — stem and branch both in full sixfold harmony.
translations.idiomatic: It cannot equal jichou-jiazi — stem and branch both in full sixfold harmony.

sentences.zh: 允一元三統之期，合五紀九章之會，共帝堯同其數，與皇唐比其蹤。

translations.literal: It fulfills the period of the one origin and three systems, joins the conjunction of five epochs and nine chapters — sharing Yao's number and comparing Tang's traces.
translations.idiomatic: It fulfills the period of the one origin and three systems and joins the conjunction of five epochs and nine chapters — sharing Emperor Yao's number and comparing with august Tang's traces.

sentences.zh: 信所謂皇哉唐哉，唐哉皇哉者矣。」

translations.literal: Truly it is what is called 'How glorious Tang! How glorious how glorious!'"
translations.idiomatic: Truly this is what is meant by 'How glorious is Tang! How glorious, how glorious!'"

sentences.zh: 仍諷齊王暕率百官拜表奉賀。

translations.literal: He also urged the Prince of Qi Yang Yong to lead the hundred officials in bowing with a memorial to offer congratulations.
translations.idiomatic: He also urged the Prince of Qi Yang Yong to lead the hundred officials in submitting a memorial of congratulation.

sentences.zh: 後熒惑守太微者數旬，時繕修宮室，征役繁重，充乃上表稱「陛下修德，熒惑退舍」。

translations.literal: Later Mars lingered in guarding the Tail Enclosure for several tens of days; at the time palace buildings were being repaired and corvée labor was heavy. Chong then submitted a memorial saying, "Your majesty cultivates virtue; Mars withdraws from its station."
translations.idiomatic: Later Mars lingered in the Tail Enclosure for several weeks. At the time the palace was under repair and corvée labor was crushing. Chong submitted a memorial claiming, "Your Majesty cultivates virtue, and Mars has withdrawn from its station."

sentences.zh: 百僚畢賀。

translations.literal: The hundred officials all congratulated.
translations.idiomatic: All the officials offered congratulations.

sentences.zh: 帝大喜，前後賞賜將萬計。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly pleased; rewards before and after approached ten thousand in count.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was delighted and showered him with rewards that soon approached ten thousand items in all.

sentences.zh: 時軍國多務，充候帝意欲有所為，便奏稱天文見象，須有改作，以是取媚於上。

translations.literal: At the time military and state affairs were many; Chong watched the emperor's intent for whatever he wished to do and would memorial that heavenly signs appeared requiring changes — thus currying favor with his superiors.
translations.idiomatic: Military and civil affairs pressed on every side. Chong watched what the emperor wished to undertake and would memorial that the heavens showed signs requiring some new measure, thereby currying favor at court.

sentences.zh: 大業六年，遷內史舍人。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Daye, he was transferred to Secretary within the Palace.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Daye he was promoted to Secretary within the Palace.

sentences.zh: 從征遼東，拜朝請大夫、秘書少監。

translations.literal: He followed the expedition to Liaodong and was appointed Gentleman for Court Appearance and Junior Supervisor of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He accompanied the Liaodong campaign and was appointed Gentleman for Court Appearance and Junior Supervisor of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 後天下大亂，帝初罹雁門之厄，又盜賊益起，心不自安。

translations.literal: Later the realm fell into great disorder; the emperor had first suffered the crisis at Yanmen, and bandits rose ever more — his heart was not at ease.
translations.idiomatic: Later the empire plunged into chaos. The emperor had barely survived the crisis at Yanmen, and rebels were rising everywhere; he could not set his mind at rest.

sentences.zh: 充復托天文，上表陳嘉瑞以媚上曰：

translations.literal: Chong again relied on astronomy, submitting a memorial citing auspicious omens to flatter the emperor, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Chong again invoked astronomy and submitted a memorial praising auspicious omens to flatter the throne, saying:

sentences.zh: 伏惟陛下握錄圖而馭黔首，提萬善而化八紘，以百姓為心，匪一人受慶，先天罔違所欲，後天必奉其時。

translations.literal: I humbly consider that your majesty grasps the recorded chart and steers the black-haired people, lifts ten thousand goods to transform the eight cords, takes the common people as his heart — not one man alone receives blessing; what Heaven affirms beforehand none may disobey; what comes after Heaven must follow its season.
translations.idiomatic: I humbly consider that Your Majesty grasps the celestial chart and guides the black-haired people, lifts every good to transform the eight directions, and takes the common people to heart — not one man alone receives blessing. What Heaven affirms beforehand none may oppose; what Heaven ordains afterward must be met in its season.

sentences.zh: 是以初膺寶曆，正當上元之紀；

translations.literal: Thus at first receiving the sacred calendar, it rightly falls in the epoch of the upper origin;
translations.idiomatic: Thus, at first receiving the sacred calendar, you rightly stand in the epoch of the upper origin;

sentences.zh: 乾之初九，又與本命符會。

translations.literal: Qian's initial nine moreover matches the tally of his natal fate.
translations.idiomatic: the initial nine of Qian moreover coincides with the tally of your natal fate.

sentences.zh: 斯則聖人冥契，故能動合天經。

translations.literal: This is the sage's hidden accord; therefore he can act in harmony with Heaven's norm.
translations.idiomatic: This is the sage's secret accord with Heaven; therefore your every movement aligns with its law.

sentences.zh: 謹案去年已來，玄象星瑞，毫釐無爽。

translations.literal: Respectfully examined: since last year, dark signs and star auspices — not a hair's breadth awry.
translations.idiomatic: Respectfully examined: since last year the dark signs and stellar omens have not deviated by a hair's breadth.

sentences.zh: 謹錄尤異，上天降祥、破突厥等狀七事。

translations.literal: Respectfully recorded the outstanding marvels: seven items including Heaven sending blessing and destroying the Turks.
translations.idiomatic: I respectfully record the most extraordinary instances — seven matters in all, including Heaven sending blessings and the destruction of the Turks.

sentences.zh: 其一，去八月二十八日夜，大流星如鬥，出王良北，正落突厥營，聲如崩牆。

translations.literal: First: on the night of the twenty-eighth day of the eighth month last year, a great meteor like the Dipper emerged north of Wang Liang and fell straight into the Turk camp, sounding like a collapsing wall.
translations.idiomatic: First: on the night of the twenty-eighth of the eighth month last year, a great meteor the size of the Dipper emerged north of Wang Liang and fell straight into the Turk camp with a sound like a wall collapsing.

sentences.zh: 其二，八月二十九日夜，復有大流星如鬥，出羽林，向北流，正當北方。

translations.literal: Second: on the night of the twenty-ninth of the eighth month, again a great meteor like the Dipper emerged from the Feathered Forest, flowed north — directly toward the north.
translations.idiomatic: Second: on the night of the twenty-ninth of the eighth month, another great meteor the size of the Dipper emerged from the Feathered Forest and streamed north, straight toward the northern quarter.

sentences.zh: 依占，頻二夜流星墜賊所，賊必敗散。

translations.literal: According to divination, two nights in succession meteors fell on the rebels' place — the rebels must be defeated and scattered.
translations.idiomatic: By divination, when meteors fall on the enemy's position two nights in succession, the rebels are sure to be broken and scattered.

sentences.zh: 其三，九月四日夜，頻有兩星大如鬥，出北斗魁，向東北流。

translations.literal: Third: on the night of the fourth of the ninth month, repeatedly two stars large as the Dipper emerged from the handle of the Big Dipper, flowing northeast.
translations.idiomatic: Third: on the night of the fourth of the ninth month, two stars as large as the Dipper repeatedly emerged from the handle of the Northern Dipper and streamed northeast.

sentences.zh: 依占，北斗主殺伐，賊必破敗。

translations.literal: According to divination, the Big Dipper governs killing — the rebels must be broken and defeated.
translations.idiomatic: By divination, the Northern Dipper governs slaughter; the rebels are certain to be shattered.

sentences.zh: 其四，歲星主福德，頻行京都二處分野。

translations.literal: Fourth: Jupiter governs fortune and virtue, repeatedly traversing the two territorial divisions of the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Fourth: Jupiter governs fortune and virtue and has repeatedly crossed the two territorial divisions of the capital.

sentences.zh: 依占，國家之福。

translations.literal: According to divination — the state's blessing.
translations.idiomatic: By divination this is the state's blessing.

sentences.zh: 其五，去七月內，熒惑守羽林，九月七日已退舍。

translations.literal: Fifth: within the seventh month last year Mars guarded the Feathered Forest; on the seventh of the ninth month it had already withdrawn from its station.
translations.idiomatic: Fifth: within the seventh month last year Mars lingered in the Feathered Forest; by the seventh of the ninth month it had already withdrawn.

sentences.zh: 依占，不出三日，賊必敗散。

translations.literal: According to divination, within three days the rebels must be defeated and scattered.
translations.idiomatic: By divination, within three days the rebels are sure to be broken and scattered.

sentences.zh: 其六，去年十一月二十日夜，有流星赤如火，從東北向西南，落賊帥盧明月營，破其橦車。

translations.literal: Sixth: on the night of the twentieth of the eleventh month last year, a meteor red as fire went from northeast toward southwest, falling on the rebel leader Lu Mingyue's camp and smashing his battering rams.
translations.idiomatic: Sixth: on the night of the twentieth of the eleventh month last year, a meteor red as fire passed from northeast to southwest and fell on the camp of the rebel chief Lu Mingyue, destroying his siege towers.

sentences.zh: 其七，十二月十五日夜，通漢鎮北有赤氣互北方，突厥將亡之應也。

translations.literal: Seventh: on the night of the fifteenth of the twelfth month, north of Tonghan Pass red vapor filled the north — the omen that the Turks would perish.
translations.idiomatic: Seventh: on the night of the fifteenth of the twelfth month, north of Tonghan Pass red vapor stretched across the northern sky — the sign that the Turks would perish.

sentences.zh: 依勘《城錄》，河南、洛陽並當甲子，與乾元初九爻及上元甲子符合。

translations.literal: According to examination of the 《City Record》, Henan and Luoyang both fall on jiazi, matching Qian's initial nine line and the upper origin's jiazi.
translations.idiomatic: According to examination of the 《City Record》, both Henan and Luoyang fall on jiazi, in accord with the initial nine line of Qian and the jiazi of the upper origin.

sentences.zh: 此是福地，永無所慮。

translations.literal: This is a blessed land — forever nothing to fear.
translations.idiomatic: These are blessed lands; you need never fear for them.

sentences.zh: 旋觀往政，側聞前古，彼則異時間出，今則一朝總萃。

translations.literal: Turning to view past reigns and overhearing antiquity — there such things appeared at different times; now they gather in one morning.
translations.idiomatic: Looking back at past reigns and recalling antiquity, such omens there appeared at separate times; now they have gathered in a single morning.

sentences.zh: 豈非天贊有道，助殲凶孽？

translations.literal: Is this not Heaven aiding the Way and helping destroy vicious evildoers?
translations.idiomatic: Is this not Heaven aiding the righteous Way and helping annihilate vicious rebels?

sentences.zh: 方清九夷於東濊，沉五狄於北溟，告成岱岳，無為汾水。

translations.literal: About to clear the nine Yi in the eastern marshes and sink the five Di in the northern sea, proclaim completion at Mount Tai, and rule without action at Fen River.
translations.idiomatic: You are about to pacify the nine Yi in the eastern marshes and sink the five Di in the northern sea, proclaim your achievement on Mount Tai, and rule in effortless ease beside the Fen River.

sentences.zh: 書奏，帝大悅，超拜秘書令。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted, the emperor was greatly pleased and promoted him in exceptional leap to Secretary Chief.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial was submitted, the emperor was delighted and promoted him by exceptional leap to Secretary-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 親待逾昵，每欲征討，充皆預知之，乃假託星象，獎成帝意，在位者皆切患之。

translations.literal: Favored ever more intimately — whenever the emperor wished to campaign, Chong foreknew it and would falsely cite star signs to encourage the emperor's intent; those in office all deeply resented it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor favored him ever more closely. Whenever he wished to launch a campaign, Chong would anticipate it and, feigning astral signs, encourage his designs. Everyone at court deeply resented him.

sentences.zh: 宇文化及弑逆之際，並誅充。

translations.literal: At the moment of Yuwen Huaji's regicide, Chong was killed along with the others.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuwen Huaji carried out his regicide, Chong was executed along with the rest.

sentences.zh: 李雄，勃海蓚人也。

translations.literal: Li Xiong was a native of Liu in Bohai.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xiong was a native of Liu in Bohai.

sentences.zh: 父棠，名列《誠義傳》。

translations.literal: His father Tang is listed in the 《Biographies of Sincerity and Righteousness》.
translations.idiomatic: His father Tang is recorded in the 《Biographies of Sincerity and Righteousness》.

sentences.zh: 雄少慷慨，有壯志。

translations.literal: In youth Xiong was generous and had great resolve.
translations.idiomatic: In youth Xiong was open-handed and ambitious.

sentences.zh: 弱冠，從周武帝平齊，以功授帥都督。

translations.literal: At weak adulthood he followed Emperor Wu of Zhou in pacifying Qi and for merit was appointed Commandant of the Guards.
translations.idiomatic: At his coming of age he followed Emperor Wu of Zhou in pacifying Qi and, for merit, was appointed Commandant of the Guards.

sentences.zh: 隋文帝作相，從韋孝寬破尉遲迥，拜上開府，賜爵建昌縣公。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen of Sui served as chancellor, he followed Wei Xiaokuan in defeating Yuwen Yong and was appointed Senior Captain Opening Office, enfeoffed as Duke of Jianchang county.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen of Sui was chancellor, he followed Wei Xiaokuan in defeating Yuwen Yong, was appointed Senior Captain Opening Office, and was enfeoffed as Duke of Jianchang county.

sentences.zh: 伐陳之後，以功進位大將軍。

translations.literal: After the campaign against Chen, for merit he advanced to Grand General.
translations.idiomatic: After the campaign against Chen he was promoted to Grand General for his achievements.

sentences.zh: 曆郴江二州刺史，並有能名。

translations.literal: He served as prefect of Chen and Jiang prefectures, in both cases gaining renown for ability.
translations.idiomatic: He served as prefect of Chen and Jiang prefectures and in both posts earned a reputation for competence.

sentences.zh: 後坐事免。

translations.literal: Later he was dismissed for an offense.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was dismissed for an offense.

sentences.zh: 漢王諒之反，煬帝將發幽州兵討之。

translations.literal: When Prince Han Yang Liang rebelled, Emperor Yang was about to dispatch Youzhou troops to suppress him.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Han Yang Liang rebelled, Emperor Yang was about to mobilize the Youzhou army to suppress him.

sentences.zh: 時竇抗為幽州總管，帝恐其貳，問可任者於楊素。

translations.literal: At the time Dou Kang was Youzhou General-in-Chief; the emperor feared he would waver and asked Yang Su who could be trusted.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Dou Kang was General-in-Chief of Youzhou. The emperor feared he might defect and asked Yang Su whom he could trust.

sentences.zh: 素遂進雄，授上大將軍，拜廉州刺史。

translations.literal: Su thereupon recommended Xiong; he was appointed Senior Grand General and made Inspector of Lian prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Su thereupon recommended Xiong, who was appointed Senior Grand General and Inspector of Lian prefecture.

sentences.zh: 馳至幽州，止傳舍，召募得千餘人。

translations.literal: Riding swiftly to Youzhou, he stopped at the relay station and recruited over a thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: He rode swiftly to Youzhou, lodged at the relay station, and recruited more than a thousand men.

sentences.zh: 抗恃素貴，不時相見。

translations.literal: Kang relied on Su's prestige and did not come to see him promptly.
translations.idiomatic: Kang, relying on Su's prestige, did not come to see him promptly.

sentences.zh: 雄遣人諭之，後二日，抗從鐵騎二千來詣雄所。

translations.literal: Xiong sent someone to instruct him; two days later Kang came to Xiong's quarters with two thousand armored cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: Xiong sent a messenger to summon him. Two days later Kang arrived at Xiong's quarters with two thousand armored horsemen.

sentences.zh: 雄伏甲禽抗，悉發幽州兵步騎三萬，自井陘討諒。

translations.literal: Xiong hid armed men and seized Kang, then mobilized all Youzhou infantry and cavalry — thirty thousand — and from Jingxing marched to attack Liang.
translations.idiomatic: Xiong concealed armed men and seized Kang, then mobilized all thirty thousand infantry and cavalry of Youzhou and marched from Jingxing to attack Liang.

sentences.zh: 遷幽州總管。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Youzhou General-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed General-in-Chief of Youzhou.

sentences.zh: 尋徵拜戶部尚書。

translations.literal: Soon summoned and appointed Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was summoned and appointed Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 雄明辯有器幹，帝甚任之。

translations.literal: Xiong was clear in debate and had capacity; the emperor greatly entrusted him.
translations.idiomatic: Xiong was sharp in debate and capable in office; the emperor relied on him heavily.

sentences.zh: 新羅嘗遣使朝貢，雄至朝堂與語，因問其冠制所由。

translations.literal: Silla once sent envoys with tribute; Xiong met them at court and conversed, thereby asking the origin of their crown form.
translations.idiomatic: Silla once sent envoys with tribute. Xiong met them in the audience hall and, in conversation, asked the origin of their style of cap.

sentences.zh: 其使者曰：「古弁遺象，安有大國君子不識？」

translations.literal: The envoy said: "It is the ancient cap's surviving image — how could a great state's gentleman not know it?"
translations.idiomatic: The envoy said, "It is the surviving form of the ancient cap — how could a gentleman of a great state fail to recognize it?"

sentences.zh: 雄因曰：「中國無禮，求諸四夷。」

translations.literal: Xiong then said: "When China lacks rites, one seeks them among the four barbarians."
translations.idiomatic: Xiong then said, "When China lacks ritual, one must seek it among the four barbarians."

sentences.zh: 使者曰：「自至已來，此言外未見無禮。」

translations.literal: The envoy said: "Since arriving, outside this remark I have seen no lack of rites."
translations.idiomatic: The envoy said, "Since I arrived, apart from this remark I have seen no want of ritual."

sentences.zh: 憲司以雄失辭，奏劾其事，竟坐免。

translations.literal: The censorate held that Xiong had misspoken; they memorialized impeaching the matter, and in the end he was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: The censorate held that Xiong had misspoken, memorialized to impeach him, and in the end he was dismissed from office.

sentences.zh: 俄而復職。

translations.literal: Before long he was restored to office.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was restored to office.

sentences.zh: 從幸江都，帝以仗衛不整，顧雄部伍之。

translations.literal: Following the emperor to Jiangdu, because the guard retinue was not in order the emperor looked to Xiong's command.
translations.idiomatic: On the journey to Jiangdu, because the guard retinue was disorderly, the emperor turned to Xiong to put his troops in order.

sentences.zh: 雄立指麾，六軍肅然。

translations.literal: Xiong stood directing — the six armies were sternly ordered.
translations.idiomatic: Xiong stood directing them, and the six armies fell into perfect order.

sentences.zh: 帝大悅曰：「公真武侯才也。」

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly pleased and said: "You truly have Marquis Wu's talent."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was delighted and said, "You truly have the talent of the Marquis of Wu."

sentences.zh: 尋轉右候衛大將軍。

translations.literal: Soon transferred to Grand General of the Right Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was transferred to Grand General of the Right Guard.

sentences.zh: 復坐事除名。

translations.literal: Again dismissed and name struck off for an offense.
translations.idiomatic: Again he was punished for an offense and struck from the rolls.

sentences.zh: 遼東之役，帝令從軍自效，因從來護兒自東萊將指滄海。

translations.literal: In the Liaodong campaign the emperor ordered him to follow the army to redeem himself; he followed Lai Hu'er from Donglai intending to cross the blue sea.
translations.idiomatic: During the Liaodong campaign the emperor ordered him to follow the army and redeem himself. He accompanied Lai Hu'er from Donglai, intending to strike across the open sea.

sentences.zh: 會楊玄感反于黎陽，帝疑之，詔鎖雄送行在所。

translations.literal: When Yang Xuangan rebelled at Liyang, the emperor suspected him and ordered Xiong shackled and sent to the traveling palace.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Xuangan rebelled at Liyang, the emperor grew suspicious and ordered Xiong shackled and sent to the traveling palace.

sentences.zh: 雄殺使亡歸玄感，玄感每與計焉。

translations.literal: Xiong killed his escort and fled back to Xuangan; Xuangan consulted him on every plan.
translations.idiomatic: Xiong killed his escort and fled to Xuangan, who consulted him on every plan.

sentences.zh: 及玄感敗，伏誅，籍沒其家。

translations.literal: When Xuangan was defeated, he was executed by decapitation and his household was confiscated.
translations.idiomatic: When Xuangan was defeated, Xiong was executed and his household goods were confiscated.

sentences.zh: 論曰：隋文肇基王業，劉昉實啟其謀，于時當軸執鈞，物無異論。

translations.literal: The discussion says: Emperor Wen of Sui began the royal enterprise — Liu Fang truly opened the plot; at that time holding the axle and wielding the steelyard, none among things had divergent opinion.
translations.idiomatic: The historians remark: When Emperor Wen of Sui laid the foundations of his rule, Liu Fang truly opened the conspiracy. At that time he held the reins of power, and no one disputed his authority.

sentences.zh: 不能忘身急病，以義斷恩，方乃慮難求全，偷安懷祿。

translations.literal: Unable to forget himself and hurry to illness, to break with kin on grounds of righteousness — instead he considered difficulty and sought completeness, stealing ease and cherishing emolument.
translations.idiomatic: He could not forget himself in urgent peril and sever ties of favor on grounds of righteousness. Instead he sought safety amid difficulty and clung to ease and salary.

sentences.zh: 其在周也，靡忠貞之節；

translations.literal: In Zhou there was no loyal, steadfast integrity;
translations.idiomatic: Under the Zhou he showed no loyal steadfastness;

sentences.zh: 其奉隋也，愧竭命之誠。

translations.literal: serving Sui, he was shamed at lacking devotion unto death.
translations.idiomatic: serving the Sui, he lacked the devotion of giving his life to the end.

sentences.zh: 非義掩其前功，蓄怨興其後釁，而望不陷刑辟，保貴全生，難矣。

translations.literal: Using injustice to cover his earlier merit, hoarding resentment to raise later strife — yet hoping not to fall under punishment, to preserve nobility and complete life — difficult!
translations.idiomatic: He used injustice to cover his earlier achievements and stored up resentment that bred later strife, yet hoped to escape punishment, preserve his rank, and keep his life whole — a vain hope indeed.

sentences.zh: 柳裘、皇甫績，因人成事，好亂樂禍，大運光啟，並參樞要。

translations.literal: Liu Qiu and Huang Fuji achieved success through others, loved chaos and delighted in disaster; when the great fortune brightly opened, each joined pivotal posts.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Qiu and Huang Fuji rose through others' efforts, loved turmoil and delighted in calamity, and when the great mandate dawned each took a place among the inner circle.

sentences.zh: 斯固在人欲其悅己，在我欲其罵人，理自然也。

translations.literal: This is naturally so: others wish those who please them; I wish those who curse others — so states reasoning.
translations.idiomatic: This is only natural: others want those who please them; I want those who will curse others on my behalf — such is the way of the world.

sentences.zh: 晏嬰有言曰：「一心可以事百君，百心不可以事一君。」

translations.literal: Yan Ying had a saying: "One heart can serve a hundred lords; a hundred hearts cannot serve one lord."
translations.idiomatic: Yan Ying once said, "One loyal heart can serve a hundred lords; a hundred hearts cannot serve one lord."

sentences.zh: 於昉等見之矣。

translations.literal: In Fang and the others this is seen.
translations.idiomatic: In Fang and his like we see the truth of it.

sentences.zh: 郭衍，文皇締構之始，當爪牙之寄；

translations.literal: Guo Yan — at the start of Emperor Wen's founding, he bore the charge of fangs and claws;
translations.idiomatic: Guo Yan, at the beginning of Emperor Wen's founding, bore the charge of fang and claw;

sentences.zh: 煬帝經綸之際，參心膂之謀。

translations.literal: in Emperor Yang's ordering of the realm, he shared the heart-and-backbone counsel.
translations.idiomatic: in Emperor Yang's ordering of the realm, shared counsel at the ruler's right hand.

sentences.zh: 而如脂如韋，以水濟水，君所謂可，亦曰可焉，君所謂不，亦曰不焉，功雖居多，名不見重。

translations.literal: Yet soft as grease, supple as leather, like water added to water — what the lord calls acceptable, he too says acceptable; what the lord calls not, he too says not; though merit was mostly his, his name was not regarded as weighty.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he was soft as grease and pliant as leather, like water poured on water: what the lord approved, he approved; what the lord rejected, he rejected. Though his achievements were many, his reputation carried little weight.

sentences.zh: 然則立身行道，可不慎歟！

translations.literal: Thus in establishing oneself and walking the Way — can one not be cautious!
translations.idiomatic: How careful one must be, then, in establishing oneself and walking the Way!

sentences.zh: 語曰：「無為權首，將受其咎。」

translations.literal: The saying goes: "Do not be the head of authority — one will receive its calamity."
translations.idiomatic: The proverb says, "Do not be the foremost wielder of power, or you will bear its punishment."

sentences.zh: 又曰：「無始禍，無兆亂。」

translations.literal: Also: "Do not begin calamity, do not herald chaos."
translations.idiomatic: And again: "Do not be the first to bring calamity, nor the first sign of disorder."

sentences.zh: 夫忠為令德，施非其人尚或不可，況托足邪徑，又不得其人者歟！

translations.literal: Loyalty is the foremost virtue; to bestow it on the wrong person may still be impossible — how much more to set foot on an evil path and moreover not find the right person!
translations.idiomatic: Loyalty is the foremost virtue; to bestow it on the wrong person may still be unwise — how much more to set foot on a crooked path and fail to find the right master!

sentences.zh: 張衡奪宗之計，實兆其謀，夫動不以順，能無及於此也？

translations.literal: Zhang Heng's plan to seize the succession truly heralded his scheming — actions not based on righteousness, could they fail to reach this?
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Heng's plot to seize the succession was itself the first omen of his treachery. When action is not grounded in righteousness, can disaster fail to follow?

sentences.zh: 楊汪以學業自許，其終不令，惜乎！

translations.literal: Yang Wang prided himself on learning — his end was not good; alas!
translations.idiomatic: Yang Wang prided himself on scholarship, yet came to a bad end — a pity indeed!

sentences.zh: 裴蘊素懷奸險，巧於附會，作威作福，唯利是視，滅亡之禍，其可免乎！

translations.literal: Pei Yun always harbored treacherous cunning, skillful at joining factions, making might and making blessing, viewing profit alone — could the calamity of extinction be escaped!
translations.idiomatic: Pei Yun always harbored treacherous designs, was skilled at attaching himself to power, made might and made blessing, and looked to profit alone — could he escape the calamity of ruin?

sentences.zh: 袁充少在江東，初以警悟見許，委質隋氏，更以玄象自矜，要求時幸，幹進附入，變動星占，謬增晷景，厚誣天道，亂常侮眾。

translations.literal: Yuan Chong in youth was in Jiangdong, first praised for alert comprehension; pledging to the Sui clan, he further prided himself on dark signs, sought the age's favor, schemed advancement and attached himself, altered star divination, falsely increased gnomon shadows, gravely slandering Heaven's Way, overturning constants and insulting the multitude.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Chong spent his youth in the Jiangdong region and was first praised for quick wit. Having pledged himself to the Sui, he prided himself on celestial lore, courted the favor of the times, schemed for advancement, altered star divination, falsely lengthened the gnomon's shadow, grossly slandered Heaven's Way, and overturned the norms to deceive the people.

sentences.zh: 刑茲勿舍，其在斯乎！

translations.literal: Punish this and do not spare — is it not here!
translations.idiomatic: When punishment is due, let it not be spared — is that not the case here?

sentences.zh: 李雄斯言為玷，取譏夷翟，以亂從亂，何救誅夷。

translations.literal: Li Xiong's words were a stain, drawing ridicule from barbarians; following chaos with chaos — how could execution be spared!
translations.idiomatic: Li Xiong's remark was a disgrace that drew the scorn of barbarians. Having joined rebellion with rebellion, what could save him from execution?
